1250.chapter: Center of Mass, Momentum and Collision
1250.text: If the linear momentum is increased by $50 \%$, then kinetic energy will increase by
1250.sol:
Kinetic energy of a body, $K=\frac{p^2}{2 m}$ where $p$ is the momentum of the body and $m$ is the mass of the body
$p^{\prime}=p+\frac{50}{100} p=\frac{3}{2} p$
Assuming $m$ remains constant
$\therefore \frac{K^{\prime}}{K}=\left(\frac{p^{\prime}}{p}\right)^2=\frac{9}{4}$
$\%$ increase in kinetic energy $=\frac{K^{\prime}-K}{K} \times 100 \%$
$=\left(\frac{K^{\prime}}{K}-1\right) \times 100 \%=\left(\frac{9}{4}-1\right) \times 100 \%=125 \%$

1543.text: A cart has mass 2 metric tone and sand of 1 metric tone is inside the cart. Now a force of $10 \mathrm{~N}$ is applied on cart and sand starts to leak with rate of $0.5 \mathrm{~kg} / \mathrm{s}$. What is the velocity of cart when total sand has come out from the cart?
1543.sol:
Mass of the cart with sand changes then its acceleration also changes.
$a=\frac{F}{m}=\frac{F}{m_0-\mu t}$
where $m$ is mass of system at time $t$,
$\begin{aligned} & m=m_0-\mu t \\ & a=\frac{F}{m_0-\mu t} \quad \text{$ or $} \quad \frac{d v}{d t}=\frac{F}{m_0-\mu t}\end{aligned} \begin{aligned} & \int_0^v d v=F \int_0^t \frac{d t}{m_0-\mu t} \\ & v=\frac{F}{\mu} \ln \left(\frac{m_0}{m_0-\mu t}\right)\end{aligned}$
Here $F=10 \mathrm{~N} ; \mu=0.5 \mathrm{~kg} / \mathrm{s}m_0=2$ metric tone $m_0-\mu t=1$ metric tone
$\therefore \quad v=\frac{10}{0.5} \ln (2)=20 \times 0.693=13.86 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$

8707.text: If a real valued function $f$ is defined by $f(x)=\frac{a x+\sqrt{a^2-x^2}}{b x}$, then $f$ is
8707.sol:
$f(x)=\frac{a x+\sqrt{x^2-a^2}}{b x}$
Then $f^{\prime}(x)=\frac{-a^2}{b x^2 \sqrt{x^2-a^2}}$
if $b > 0 \Rightarrow f^{\prime}(x) < 0 \Rightarrow f(x)$ is decreasing
$\Rightarrow f(x)$ is one-one.
if $b < 0 \Rightarrow f^{\prime}(x) > 0 \Rightarrow f(x)$ is increasing
$\Rightarrow f(x)$ is one-one.
Now, let $y=\frac{a x+\sqrt{a^2-x^2}}{b x}\begin{aligned}
& \Rightarrow(b x y-a x)^2=a^2-x^2 \\
& \Rightarrow x^2(b y-a)^2+x^2=a^2 \\
& \Rightarrow x^2=\frac{a^2}{1+(b y-a)^2} \\
& \Rightarrow x= \pm \frac{a}{\sqrt{1+(b y-a)^2}} \quad\left[\because 1+(b y-a)^2 > 0\right] \\
& \therefore y \in \mathbb{R}
\end{aligned}$
So, $\mathrm{f}(\mathrm{x})$ is onto also.

14253.text:
Consider the two following statements $A$ and $B$, and identify the correct choice given in the answers :
(A) In photovoltaic cells the photoelectric current produced is not proportional to the intensity of incident light.
(B) In gas filled photoemissive cells, the velocity of photoelectrons depends on the wavelength of the incident radiation.
14253.sol:
In photovoltaic cells the photoelectric current produced is proportional to the intensity of incident light, so statement $A$ is false.
The velocity of photoelectrons depends on the maximum kinetic energy of photoelectrons, which depends on the frequency and hence on the wavelength of incident radiation, so statement $B$ is true.

19885.subject: Chemistry
19885.text: The temperature $(\mathrm{T})$ and rate constant $(\mathrm{k})$ for a first order reaction $\mathrm{R} \rightarrow \mathrm{P}$, was found to follow the equation $\log \mathrm{k}=-(2000) \dfrac{1}{\mathrm{ T}}+8.0$. The pre-exponential factor '$\mathrm{A}$' and activation energy $\mathrm{E}_{\mathrm{a}}$, respectively are: [Given: $\mathrm{R}=8.314 \mathrm{ J} \mathrm{ K}^{-1} \mathrm{ mol}^{-1}$]
19885.sol:
The Arrhenius equation is given by $k = A e^{-E_a / (RT)}$.

Taking the logarithm on both sides, we get $\log k = \log A - \dfrac{E_a}{2.303 RT}$.

Comparing this with the given equation $\log k = -2000 \left( \dfrac{1}{T} \right) + 8.0$, we identify the slope and the intercept.

The slope is $-\dfrac{E_a}{2.303 R} = -2000$.

Therefore, $E_a = 2000 \times 2.303 \times R = 2000 \times 2.303 \times 8.314 \text{ J mol}^{-1}$.

$E_a = 4606 \times 8.314 \approx 38294 \text{ J mol}^{-1} = 38.3 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$.

The intercept is $\log A = 8.0$.

Therefore, $A = 10^8 \text{ s}^{-1}$.

Answer: $1 \times 10^8 \mathrm{ s}^{-1} \text{ and } 38.3 \mathrm{ kJ} \mathrm{ mol}^{-1}$

19980.subject: Chemistry
19980.text: The Crystal Field Stabilisation energy of (i) $[\text{CoF}_6]^{3-}$ and (ii) $[\text{Fe}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_6]^{3+}$ are ----- and ------- respectively.
19980.sol:
For the complex $[\text{CoF}_6]^{3-}$:
The oxidation state of Co is $+3$. The electronic configuration of $\text{Co}^{3+}$ is $3d^6$.
Since $\text{F}^-$ is a weak field ligand, the complex is high-spin. The electrons are distributed in the $t_{2g}$ and $e_g$ orbitals as $t_{2g}^4 e_g^2$.
$\text{CFSE} = (-0.4 \times n_{t_{2g}} + 0.6 \times n_{e_g}) \Delta_0$
$\text{CFSE} = (-0.4 \times 4 + 0.6 \times 2) \Delta_0 = (-1.6 + 1.2) \Delta_0 = -0.4 \Delta_0$

For the complex $[\text{Fe}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_6]^{3+}$:
The oxidation state of Fe is $+3$. The electronic configuration of $\text{Fe}^{3+}$ is $3d^5$.
Since $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ is a weak field ligand, the complex is high-spin. The electrons are distributed as $t_{2g}^3 e_g^2$.
$\text{CFSE} = (-0.4 \times 3 + 0.6 \times 2) \Delta_0 = (-1.2 + 1.2) \Delta_0 = 0 \Delta_0$

Answer: (i) $-0.4\Delta_0$ (ii) $0\ \Delta_0$

20119.text:
The $\Delta G$^o for $the reaction, \text{Cd}^{2+}($aq) + $\text{Zn}(s) \rightarrow \text{Zn}^{2+}($aq) + $\text{Cd}(s)$ is:
$\left[E^o_{\text{Cd}^{2+}/\text{Cd}} = -0.403,\ E^o_{\text{Zn}^{2+}/\text{Zn}} = -0.763\ V\right]$
20119.sol:
For the reaction $\text{Cd}^{2+}(aq) + \text{Zn}(s) \rightarrow \text{Zn}^{2+}(aq) + \text{Cd}(s)$, Zn is oxidized (anode) and $\text{Cd}^{2+}$ is reduced (cathode).

$E^{{}^{\circ}}_{\text{cell}} = E^{{}^{\circ}}_{\text{cathode}} - E^{{}^{\circ}}_{\text{anode}}$

$E^{{}^{\circ}}_{\text{cell}} = -0.403 - (-0.763) = 0.360\text{ V}$

The number of electrons transferred in the reaction is $n = 2$.

The standard Gibbs free energy change is given by:

$\Delta G^{{}^{\circ}} = -nFE^{{}^{\circ}}_{\text{cell}}$

$\Delta G^{{}^{\circ}} = -2 \times 96500 \times 0.360$

$\Delta G^{{}^{\circ}} = -69480\text{ J} = -69.48\text{ kJ}$

Rounding to one decimal place, $\Delta G^{{}^{\circ}} \approx -69.5\text{ kJ}$.

Answer: $-69.5\ kJ$

options: For a solvent, $\quad K_b=\dfrac{R \times M_1 \times T_b^2}{1000 \times \Delta \text{ Hvap }}\left(\mathrm{R}=\right.$ Gas constant, $M_1=$ Molar mass of solvent, $T_b=B. P$ of the solvent $)$

20645.sol:
(1) Correct: $K_b = \dfrac{R \times M_1 \times T_b^2}{1000 \times \Delta H_{vap}}$ is the standard thermodynamic expression for the ebullioscopic constant, where $R$ is the gas constant, $M_1$ is the molar mass of solvent, $T_b$ is the boiling point of pure solvent, and $\Delta H_{vap}$ is the molar enthalpy of vaporization.

(2) Incorrect: A hypotonic solution has lower solute concentration. The solution with higher concentration is called hypertonic.

(3) Incorrect: 1.0 M solution has 1 mole of glucose in 1 L of solution (less than 1 kg of solvent), while 1.0 m solution has 1 mole in exactly 1 kg of solvent. Hence 1.0 M is more concentrated than 1.0 m, not less.

(4) Incorrect: $CS_2$ + Acetone shows positive deviation from Raoult's law (weaker A-B interactions), forming a minimum boiling azeotrope, not a maximum boiling azeotrope.

The correct statement is (1).

20861.subject: Chemistry
20861.text: The correct option for free expansion of an ideal gas under adiabatic condition is:
20861.sol:
Free expansion of an ideal gas occurs against vacuum, which implies that the external pressure $P_{ext} = 0$.

The work done in the process is given by $w = -\int P_{ext} dV$. Since $P_{ext} = 0$, the work done $w = 0$.

The process is stated to be adiabatic, which means there is no heat exchange with the surroundings, so $q = 0$.

According to the first law of thermodynamics, $\Delta U = q + w$. Substituting $q = 0$ and $w = 0$, we get $\Delta U = 0$.

For an ideal gas, the internal energy $U$ is a function of temperature only, i.e., $U = f(T)$. Therefore, $\Delta U = n C_v \Delta T$. Since $\Delta U = 0$ and $n, C_v \neq 0$, it follows that $\Delta T = 0$.

Thus, for free expansion of an ideal gas under adiabatic conditions, $q = 0$, $w = 0$, and $\Delta T = 0$.

Answer: $\mathrm{q}=0, \quad \Delta \mathrm{T}=0, \quad \mathrm{w}=0$

21229.text: If $f(x) = \left\{ {\matrix{ {2\sin x} \text{ and } ; \text{ and } { - \pi \le x \le {{ - \pi } \over 2}} \cr {a\sin x + b} \text{ and } ; \text{ and } { - {\pi \over 2} < x < {\pi \over 2}} \cr {\cos x} \text{ and } ; \text{ and } {{\pi \over 2} \le x \le \pi } \cr } } \right.$ and it is continuous on $[-\pi, \pi]$, then
21229.sol:
For $f(x)$ to be continuous on $[-\pi, \pi]$, it must be continuous at $x = -\dfrac{\pi}{2}$ and $x = \dfrac{\pi}{2}$.

At $x = -\dfrac{\pi}{2}$, the left-hand limit equals the right-hand limit:
$\lim_{x \to -\pi/2^{-}} 2\sin x = \lim_{x \to -\pi/2^{+}} (a\sin x + b)$
$2\sin(-\pi/2) = a\sin(-\pi/2) + b$
$-2 = -a + b$ --- (1)

At $x = \dfrac{\pi}{2}$, the left-hand limit equals the right-hand limit:
$\lim_{x \to \pi/2^{-}} (a\sin x + b) = \lim_{x \to \pi/2^{+}} \cos x$
$a\sin(\pi/2) + b = \cos(\pi/2)$
$a + b = 0$ --- (2)

Adding equations (1) and (2):
$(-a + b) + (a + b) = -2 + 0$
$2b = -2 \Rightarrow b = -1$

Substituting $b = -1$ into equation (2):
$a - 1 = 0 \Rightarrow a = 1$.

Answer: $a=1$ and $b=-1$

21426.subject: Mathematics
21426.text: The length of the latus rectum of the curve represented by $x = 3(\cos t + \sin t)$ and $y = 4(\cos t - \sin t)$ is:
21426.sol:
Given parametric equations are:

$x = 3(\cos t + \sin t) \Rightarrow \dfrac{x}{3} = \cos t + \sin t$

$y = 4(\cos t - \sin t) \Rightarrow \dfrac{y}{4} = \cos t - \sin t$

Squaring and adding both equations, we get:

$\left(\dfrac{x}{3}\right)^2 + \left(\dfrac{y}{4}\right)^2 = (\cos t + \sin t)^2 + (\cos t - \sin t)^2$

$\dfrac{x^2}{9} + \dfrac{y^2}{16} = 2(\cos^2 t + \sin^2 t)$

$\dfrac{x^2}{9} + \dfrac{y^2}{16} = 2$

$\dfrac{x^2}{18} + \dfrac{y^2}{32} = 1$

This represents an ellipse with $a^2 = 18 and b^2 = 32$.

Since $b^2 \gt a^2$, the major axis lies along the y-axis.

The length of the latus rectum is given by $\dfrac{2a^2}{b}$.

Substituting the values:

Length of latus rectum $= \dfrac{2 \times 18}{\sqrt{32}} = \dfrac{36}{4\sqrt{2}} = \dfrac{9}{\sqrt{2}}$

Answer: $\dfrac{9}{\sqrt{2}}$

21449.subject: Mathematics
21449.text: If a function $f: R \rightarrow R$ is defined as $f(x)=x^2+1$, then the pre-image of -3 is
21449.sol:
The pre-image of a value $y$ under a function $f(x)$ is the set of all $x$ such that $f(x) = y$.

Given $f(x) = x^2 + 1$, we set $f(x) = -3$.

$x^2 + 1 = -3$

$x^2 = -3 - 1$

$x^2 = -4$

Since the square of any real number $x$ must be non-negative ($x^2 \geq 0$ for all $x \in R$), there is no real number $x$ such that $x^2 = -4$.

Therefore, the set of pre-images is the empty set, denoted by $\emptyset$.

Answer: $\emptyset$

22200.subject: Mathematics
22200.text: If two lines $L_1: \dfrac{x-1}{2}=\dfrac{y+1}{3}=\dfrac{z-1}{4}$ and $L_2: \dfrac{x-3}{1}=\dfrac{y-k}{2}=z$ intersect at a point, then $2 k$ is equal to
22200.sol:
The lines are given by $L_1: \dfrac{x-1}{2} = \dfrac{y+1}{3} = \dfrac{z-1}{4} = \lambda$ and $L_2: \dfrac{x-3}{1} = \dfrac{y-k}{2} = \dfrac{z}{1} = \mu$.

Any point on $L_1$ is $(2\lambda + 1, 3\lambda - 1, 4\lambda + 1)$ and any point on $L_2$ is $(\mu + 3, 2\mu + k, \mu)$.

Since the lines intersect, there exist $\lambda$ and $\mu$ such that:
$2\lambda + 1 = \mu + 3 \Rightarrow 2\lambda - \mu = 2$ (1)
$3\lambda - 1 = 2\mu + k \Rightarrow 3\lambda - 2\mu = k + 1$ (2)
$4\lambda + 1 = \mu$ (3)

Substituting (3) into (1):
$2\lambda - (4\lambda + 1) = 2 \Rightarrow -2\lambda = 3 \Rightarrow \lambda = -\dfrac{3}{2}$.

From (3), $\mu = 4(-\dfrac{3}{2}) + 1 = -6 + 1 = -5$.

Substituting $\lambda = -\dfrac{3}{2}$ and $\mu = -5$ into (2):
$3(-\dfrac{3}{2}) - 2(-5) = k + 1$
$-\dfrac{9}{2} + 10 = k + 1$
$\dfrac{11}{2} = k + 1 \Rightarrow k = \dfrac{9}{2}$.

Therefore, $2k = 2 \times \dfrac{9}{2} = 9$.

Answer: 9

22322.text: If $\mathrm{p}=\hat{i}+\hat{j}, \mathrm{q}=4 \hat{k}-\hat{j}$ and $\mathrm{r}=\hat{i}+\hat{k}$, then the unit vector in the direction of $3 \mathrm{p}+\mathrm{q}-2 \mathrm{r}$ is
22322.sol:
Given vectors are $\vec{p} = \hat{i} + \hat{j}$, $\vec{q} = -\hat{j} + 4\hat{k}$, and $\vec{r} = \hat{i} + \hat{k}$.

Calculate the vector $\vec{v} = 3\vec{p} + \vec{q} - 2\vec{r}$:

$\vec{v} = 3(\hat{i} + \hat{j}) + (-\hat{j} + 4\hat{k}) - 2(\hat{i} + \hat{k})$

$\vec{v} = (3\hat{i} + 3\hat{j}) + (-\hat{j} + 4\hat{k}) - (2\hat{i} + 2\hat{k})$

$\vec{v} = (3 - 2)\hat{i} + (3 - 1)\hat{j} + (4 - 2)\hat{k}$

$\vec{v} = \hat{i} + 2\hat{j} + 2\hat{k}$

The magnitude of vector $\vec{v}$ is $|\vec{v}| = \sqrt{1^2 + 2^2 + 2^2} = \sqrt{1 + 4 + 4} = \sqrt{9} = 3$.

The unit vector in the direction of $\vec{v}$ is $\hat{u} = \dfrac{\vec{v}}{|\vec{v}|} = \dfrac{1}{3}(\hat{i} + 2\hat{j} + 2\hat{k})$.

Answer: $\dfrac{1}{3}(\hat{i}+2 \hat{j}+2 \hat{k})$

22955.text: The average kinetic energy of a molecule in air at room temperature of $20^{{}^{\circ}} \mathrm{C}$
22955.sol:
The average kinetic energy of a molecule is given by the formula $K_{avg} = \dfrac{3}{2} k_{B} T$, where $k_{B}$ is the Boltzmann constant and $T$ is the absolute temperature in Kelvin.

Given temperature $T = 20^{{}^{\circ}} \mathrm{C} = 20 + 273.15 = 293.15 \mathrm{ K}$.

The Boltzmann constant $k_{B} \approx 1.38 \times 10^{-23} \mathrm{ J/K}$.

Substituting the values into the formula:

$K_{avg} = \dfrac{3}{2} \times (1.38 \times 10^{-23} \mathrm{ J/K}) \times 293.15 \mathrm{ K}$

$K_{avg} = 1.5 \times 1.38 \times 293.15 \times 10^{-23} \mathrm{ J}$

$K_{avg} = 2.07 \times 293.15 \times 10^{-23} \mathrm{ J}$

$K_{avg} \approx 606.82 \times 10^{-23} \mathrm{ J}$

$K_{avg} \approx 6.0682 \times 10^{-21} \mathrm{ J}$

Rounding to three significant figures, we get $6.07 \times 10^{-21} \mathrm{ J}$.

Answer: $6.07 \times 10^{-21} \mathrm{ J}$

23030.text: Current flows through uniform, square frames and their connecting wires as shown in the figure. In which case is the net magnetic field at the centre of the frame not zero?
23030.sol:
The square frame itself always produces zero net field at the centre (symmetric current paths cancel).

Cases A and B: External wires are directed radially (along diagonals) toward/away from the centre $\Rightarrow$ their line of action passes through the centre, so they produce zero field there.

Case D: Incoming and outgoing external wires are on opposite sides and symmetric $\Rightarrow$ their fields cancel at the centre.

Case C: Both external wires are collinear with the top edge and carry current in the same direction (left to right). By the right-hand rule, both produce fields pointing into the page at the centre — they add up instead of cancelling.

Net magnetic field at the centre is non-zero only in Case C.

23919.subject: Biology
23919.text: The following pedigree diagram shows the inheritance of a rare genetic disorder in a family (filled shapes depict affected individuals). Which one of the following is the most likely pattern of inheritance of the disorder?
23919.sol:
Based on the pedigree diagram, we can determine the mode of inheritance by analyzing the transmission of the trait:

1. Generation I: An affected male and an unaffected female have offspring where all daughters are affected and all sons are unaffected. This is a classic hallmark of an X-linked dominant trait. The affected father (X^D Y$) passes his affected X chromosome to all his daughters (making them $X^D X^d$, affected) and his Y chromosome to all his sons (making them $X^d Y$, unaffected).

2. Generation III: We see two more instances of an affected male mating with an unaffected female. In both families, all daughters are affected and all sons are unaffected, perfectly consistent with X-linked dominant inheritance.

3. Generation II: Affected females (who must be heterozygous, $X^D X^d$) mate with unaffected males (X^d Y$). They pass the trait to approximately half of their sons and half of their daughters, which is expected since they have a 50% chance of passing on the affected X chromosome to any child.

4. Ruling out other options:
- Y-linked: The trait appears in females, so it cannot be Y-linked.
- Mitochondrial: An affected father passes the trait to his daughters. In mitochondrial inheritance, fathers do not pass the trait to any of their children; only mothers do.
- X-linked recessive: If it were X-linked recessive, an affected father and an unaffected (non-carrier) mother would have only unaffected children (daughters would be carriers). Here, all daughters of affected fathers are affected.

Therefore, the most likely pattern of inheritance is X-linked dominant.

Answer: X-linked dominant

25485.text: Consider the family of all circles whose centers lie on the straight line $y = x .$ If this family of circles is represented by the differential equation $Py " + Qy′ + 1 = 0,$ where $P, Q$ are functions of $x, yandy′$ $\left(here{y}^{′} = \dfrac{dy}{dx}, y " = \dfrac{{d}^{2}y}{d{x}^{2}}\right)$ , then which of the following statements is (are) true ?
25485.sol:
Let required circle be
${x}^{2} + {y}^{2} + 2g\left(x + y\right) + c = 0$
Differentiation
$2x + 2y{y}^{′} + 2g\left(1 + {y}^{′}\right) = 0$
$⇒ x + y{y}^{′} + g\left(1 + {y}^{′}\right) = 0$ ...(i)
Again differentiation
$1 + y{y}^{′} + {\left(y\right)}^{2} + g\left({y}^{′}\right) = 0$ ...(ii)
Putting value of g in equation (ii),
$1 + y{y}^{′} + {\left({y}^{′}\right)}^{2} - \left(\dfrac{x + y{y}^{′}}{1 + {y}^{′}}\right){y}^{′′} = 0$
So, $P = y - x, Q = 1 + {y}^{′} + {\left({y}^{′}\right)}^{2}$
i.e., $P + Q = 1 - x + y + {y}^{′}{\left({y}^{′}\right)}^{2}$

29282.subject: Chemistry
29282.text:
For a general redox reaction
Anode : $\text{Red}_1 \rightarrow \text{Ox}_1^{n_1^+} + n_1 e^-$
Cathode : $\text{Ox}_2 + n_2 e^- \rightarrow \text{Red}_2^{n_2^-}$
Which of the following statement is incorrect ?
options: The overall reaction can be written as $n_2\text{Red}_1 + n_1\text{Ox}_2 \rightleftharpoons n_2\text{Ox}_1^{n_1^+} + n_1\text{Red}_2^{n_2^-}$
The electrons do not appear in the overall reaction because electrons produced at the anode are consumed at the cathode.
Here $n$ is the number of electrons transferred in redox reaction.
If the reaction is carried out reversibly, the electrical work done is equal to the ratio of charge and potential difference through which charge is moved.
29282.sol:
For the given redox reaction, the half-cell reactions are:
Anode: $\text{Red}_1 \rightarrow \text{Ox}_1^{n_1^+} + n_1 e^-$
Cathode: $\text{Ox}_2 + n_2 e^- \rightarrow \text{Red}_2^{n_2^-}$

To obtain the overall balanced chemical equation, we multiply the anode reaction by $n_2$ and the cathode reaction by $n_1$ so that the number of electrons lost equals the number of electrons gained:
$n_2\text{Red}_1 \rightarrow n_2\text{Ox}_1^{n_1^+} + n_1 n_2 e^-$
$n_1\text{Ox}_2 + n_1 n_2 e^- \rightarrow n_1\text{Red}_2^{n_2^-}$

Adding these gives the overall reaction:
$n_2\text{Red}_1 + n_1\text{Ox}_2 \rightleftharpoons n_2\text{Ox}_1^{n_1^+} + n_1\text{Red}_2^{n_2^-}$
Thus, statement (A) is correct.

In the overall reaction, electrons do not appear because the electrons produced at the anode are exactly consumed at the cathode. Thus, statement (B) is correct.

From the Nernst equation:
$E = E^\circ - \dfrac{RT}{nF} \ln Q = E^\circ - \dfrac{2.303 RT}{nF} \log_{10} Q$
$\dfrac{E - E^\circ}{RT/F} = -\dfrac{2.303}{n} \log_{10} Q$
The graph of $\dfrac{E - E^\circ}{RT/F}$ versus $\log_{10} Q$ is a straight line with a slope of $-\dfrac{2.303}{n}$, where $n$ is the number of electrons transferred in the balanced redox reaction. Thus, statement (C) is correct.

The electrical work done by a galvanic cell is given by the product of the total charge transferred and the cell potential (potential difference), not their ratio.
$W_{\text{electrical}} = \text{Charge} \times \text{Potential difference} = nF E_{\text{cell}}$
Thus, statement (D) is incorrect.

Answer: If the reaction is carried out reversibly, the electrical work done is equal to the ratio of charge and potential difference through which charge is moved.

It involves dissolving aluminium oxide (alumina) (obtained most often from bauxite, aluminium's chief ore, through the Bayer process) in molten cryolite, and electrolyzing the molten salt bath, typically in a purpose-built cell.

In this process carbon electrodes are used.

The following reactions take place

$2{Al}_{2}{O}_{3} + 3C \to 4Al + 3{CO}_{2}$

$=143.5 \mathrm{~g} / \mathrm{mol} \times 0.0033$ moles $=0.48 \mathrm{~g}$.

32923.subject: Mathematics
32923.text: Let $a$ be an integer such that all the real roots of the polynomial $2{x}^{5} + 5{x}^{4} + 10{x}^{3} + 10{x}^{2} + 10x + 10$ lie in the interval $\left(a, a + 1\right)$. Then, $| a |$ is equal to ______.
32923.sol:
Let $2{x}^{5} + 5{x}^{4} + 10{x}^{3} + 10{x}^{2} + 10x + 10 = f\left(x\right)$

Now $f\left(- 2\right) = - 34$ and $f\left(- 1\right) = 3$

Hence $f\left(x\right)$ has a root in $\left(- 2, - 1\right)$

Further ${f}^{'}\left(x\right) = 10{x}^{4} + 20{x}^{3} + 30{x}^{2} + 20x + 10$

$= 10{x}^{2}\left({x}^{2} + 2x + 3 + \dfrac{2}{x} + \dfrac{1}{{x}^{2}}\right)$

$= 10{x}^{2}\left[\left({x}^{2} + \dfrac{1}{{x}^{2}}\right) + 2\left(x + \dfrac{1}{x}\right) + 3\right]$

$= 10{x}^{2}\left[{\left(x + \dfrac{1}{x}\right)}^{2} - 2 + 2\left(x + \dfrac{1}{x}\right) + 3\right]$

$= 10{x}^{2}\left[{\left(x + \dfrac{1}{x} + 1\right)}^{2}\right] > 0$ for all $x$ belongs to $R$.

$f\left(x\right)$ is strictly increasing function. Since it is an odd degree polynomial it will have exactly one real root.

Hence, $f\left(x\right)$ has only one real root, so $\left|a\right| = 2$.

The point of intersection of ${y}^{2} = 2x$ and $x + y = 4$ are $\left(8, - 4\right)$ and $\left(2, 2\right)$

33751.text: Let the circles $C_1 : |z| = r$ and $C_2 : |z - 3 - 4i| = 5$, $z \in \mathbb{C}$, be such that $C_2$ lies within $C_1$. If $z_1$ moves on $C_1$, $z_2$ moves on $C_2$ and $\min |z_1 - z_2| = 2$, then $\max |z_1 - z_2|$ is equal to:
33751.sol:
The center of circle $C_1$ is $O_1(0,0)$ and its radius is $r_1 = r$.

The center of circle $C_2$ is $O_2(3,4)$ and its radius is $r_2 = 5$.

The distance between the centers of the two circles is $d = \sqrt{3^2 + 4^2} = 5$.

Since $C_2$ lies entirely within $C_1$, the minimum distance between a point on $C_1$ and a point on $C_2$ is given by $r_1 - (d + r_2)$.

We are given that $\min |z_1 - z_2| = 2$.

$r - (5 + 5) = 2 \Rightarrow r - 10 = 2 \Rightarrow r = 12$

The maximum distance between a point on $C_1$ and a point on $C_2$ is given by $r_1 + d + r_2$.

$\max |z_1 - z_2| = 12 + 5 + 5 = 22$

Answer: $22$

35438.text: If the line $y = mx + c$ is a common tangent to the hyperbola $\dfrac{{x}^{2}}{100} - \dfrac{{y}^{2}}{64} = 1$ and the circle ${x}^{2} + {y}^{2} = 36,$ then which one of the following is true?
35438.sol:
A line $y = mx + c$ is a tangent to the hyperbola $\dfrac{{x}^{2}}{{a}^{2}} - \dfrac{{y}^{2}}{{b}^{2}} = 1$ if ${c}^{2} = {a}^{2}{m}^{2} - {b}^{2}$ and the line is tangent to the circle ${x}^{2} + {y}^{2} = {r}^{2}$ is ${c}^{2} = {r}^{2}\left(1 + {m}^{2}\right) .$

Hence, for the given line and the hyperbola we have, ${c}^{2} = 100{m}^{2} - 64 . . . \left(i\right)$ and for the line and the circle, we have

${c}^{2} = 36\left(1 + {m}^{2}\right) . . . \left(ii\right)$

On comparing the above two equations, we get

$100{m}^{2} - 64 = 36 + 36{m}^{2}$

$64{m}^{2} = 100$

${m}^{2} = \dfrac{100}{64}$ $⇒ m = \dfrac{10}{8} = \dfrac{5}{4} .$

$⇒ {c}^{2} = 36\left(1 + \dfrac{25}{16}\right) = \dfrac{369}{4} .$

36545.subject: Mathematics
36545.text: A man throws a fair coin repeatedly. He gets $10$ points for each head he throws and $5$ points for each tail he throws. If the probability that he gets exactly $30$ points is $\dfrac{m}{n}$, $\gcd(m, n) = 1$, then $m + n$ is equal to:
36545.sol:
Let $h$ be the number of heads and $t$ be the number of tails obtained.

The total points obtained is $10h + 5t$.

For the man to get exactly $30$ points, we must have:

$10h + 5t = 30 \Rightarrow 2h + t = 6$

Since $h and t$ are non-negative integers, the possible pairs of $(h, t)$ are $(3, 0)$, $(2, 2)$, $(1, 4)$, and $(0, 6)$.

For each pair, the number of possible sequences of heads and tails is given by $^{h+t}C_{h}$, and the probability of any specific sequence is $\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^{h+t}$.

The total probability is the sum of the probabilities of all these mutually exclusive cases:

For $h = 3, t = 0$, the probability is $^{3}C_{3} \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^{3} = 1 \times \dfrac{1}{8} = \dfrac{8}{64}$.

For $h = 2, t = 2$, the probability is $^{4}C_{2} \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^{4} = 6 \times \dfrac{1}{16} = \dfrac{24}{64}$.

For $h = 1, t = 4$, the probability is $^{5}C_{1} \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^{5} = 5 \times \dfrac{1}{32} = \dfrac{10}{64}$.

For $h = 0, t = 6$, the probability is $^{6}C_{0} \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^{6} = 1 \times \dfrac{1}{64} = \dfrac{1}{64}$.

Total probability $= \dfrac{8}{64} + \dfrac{24}{64} + \dfrac{10}{64} + \dfrac{1}{64} = \dfrac{43}{64}$.

Thus, $m = 43 and n = 64$.

Since $\gcd(43, 64) = 1$, the fraction is in its simplest form.

$m + n = 43 + 64 = 107$.

Answer: $107$

$a < -\frac{11}{5}$

37039.subject: Mathematics
37039.text: Suppose $\mathrm{a}, \mathrm{b}, \mathrm{c}$ are in A.P. and $\mathrm{a}^{2}, 2 \mathrm{~b}^{2}, \mathrm{c}^{2}$ are in G.P. If $\mathrm{a}<\mathrm{b}<\mathrm{c}$ and $\mathrm{a}+\mathrm{b}+\mathrm{c}=1$, then $9\left(\mathrm{a}^{2}+\mathrm{b}^{2}+\mathrm{c}^{2}\right)$ is equal to $\_\_\_\_$ .
37039.sol:
Since $a, b, c$ are in A.P., we have $2b = a + c$.
With $a + b + c = 1$, we get $3b = 1$, so $b = \frac{1}{3}$ and $a + c = \frac{2}{3}$.
Since $a^2, 2b^2, c^2$ are in G.P.: $(2b^2)^2 = a^2 c^2$, giving $4b^4 = a^2c^2$.
With $b = \frac{1}{3}$: $a^2c^2 = \frac{4}{81}$.
For real values with $a < b < c$, we need $ac = -\frac{2}{9}$.
Thus $a, c$ satisfy $t^2 - \frac{2}{3}t - \frac{2}{9} = 0$, giving $t = \frac{1 \pm \sqrt{3}}{3}$. So $a = \frac{1-\sqrt{3}}{3}$, $c = \frac{1+\sqrt{3}}{3}$.
Calculating: $a^2 + c^2 = \frac{(1-\sqrt{3})^2 + (1+\sqrt{3})^2}{9} = \frac{4-2\sqrt{3}+4+2\sqrt{3}}{9} = \frac{8}{9}$.
Therefore $a^2 + b^2 + c^2 = \frac{8}{9} + \frac{1}{9} = 1$, and $9(a^2 + b^2 + c^2) = 9$.

37495.subject: Mathematics
37495.text: A data consists of $20$ observations $x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_{20}$. If $\sum_{i=1}^{20}(x_i + 5)^2 = 2500$ and $\sum_{i=1}^{20}(x_i - 5)^2 = 100$, then the ratio of mean to standard deviation of this data is:
37495.sol:
Given $\sum_{i=1}^{20}(x_i + 5)^2 = 2500$ and $\sum_{i=1}^{20}(x_i - 5)^2 = 100$.

Expanding the first equation:
$\sum_{i=1}^{20} (x_i^2 + 10x_i + 25) = 2500$
$\sum_{i=1}^{20} x_i^2 + 10 \sum_{i=1}^{20} x_i + 500 = 2500$
$\sum_{i=1}^{20} x_i^2 + 10 \sum_{i=1}^{20} x_i = 2000$ --- (1)

Expanding the second equation:
$\sum_{i=1}^{20} (x_i^2 - 10x_i + 25) = 100$
$\sum_{i=1}^{20} x_i^2 - 10 \sum_{i=1}^{20} x_i + 500 = 100$
$\sum_{i=1}^{20} x_i^2 - 10 \sum_{i=1}^{20} x_i = -400$ --- (2)

Subtracting (2) from (1):
$20 \sum_{i=1}^{20} x_i = 2400 \Rightarrow \sum_{i=1}^{20} x_i = 120$

Adding (1) and (2):
$2 \sum_{i=1}^{20} x_i^2 = 1600 \Rightarrow \sum_{i=1}^{20} x_i^2 = 800$

Mean ($\mu$) is given by:
$\mu = \dfrac{\sum_{i=1}^{20} x_i}{20} = \dfrac{120}{20} = 6$

Variance ($\sigma^2$) is given by:
$\sigma^2 = \dfrac{\sum_{i=1}^{20} x_i^2}{20} - \mu^2 = \dfrac{800}{20} - 6^2 = 40 - 36 = 4$

Standard deviation ($\sigma$) is $\sqrt{4} = 2$.

The ratio of mean to standard deviation is:
$\dfrac{\mu}{\sigma} = \dfrac{6}{2} = \dfrac{3}{1}$

Answer: $3:1$

37973.text: Let a line passing through the point $( - 1, 2, 3 )$ intersect the lines ${L}_{1}: \dfrac{x - 1}{3} = \dfrac{y - 2}{2} = \dfrac{z + 1}{- 2}$ at $M ( \alpha, \beta, \gamma )$ and ${L}_{2}: \dfrac{x + 2}{- 3} = \dfrac{y - 2}{- 2} = \dfrac{z - 1}{4}$ at $N ( a, b, c )$. Let,

${L}_{1}: \dfrac{x - 1}{3} = \dfrac{y - 2}{2} = \dfrac{z + 1}{- 2} = \lambda$

$⇒ M ( 3\lambda + 1, 2\lambda + 2, - 2\lambda - 1 ) ≡ M\left(\alpha, \beta, \gamma\right)$

$⇒ \alpha + \beta + \gamma = 3\lambda + 2$

$⇒ N ( - 3\mu - 2, - 2\mu + 2, 4\mu + 1 ) ≡ N\left(a, b, c\right)$

$⇒ a + b + c = - \mu + 1$

Now, from the above diagram, we can see $MN$ lie on the same line,

So, $\dfrac{3\lambda + 2}{- 3\mu - 1} = \dfrac{2\lambda}{- 2\mu} = \dfrac{- 2\lambda - 4}{4\mu - 2}$

Now, solving $\dfrac{3\lambda + 2}{- 3\mu - 1} = \dfrac{2\lambda}{- 2\mu}$

$⇒ 3\lambda\mu + 2\mu = 3\lambda\mu + \lambda$

$⇒ 2\mu = \lambda . . . . . . \left(i\right)$

Now, solving $\dfrac{2\lambda}{- 2\mu} = \dfrac{- 2\lambda - 4}{4\mu - 2}$ we get,

$⇒ 2\lambda\mu - \lambda = \lambda\mu + 2\mu$

$⇒ \lambda\mu = \lambda + 2\mu$

$⇒ \lambda\mu = 2\lambda$ $\left\{\text{as}2\mu = \lambda\right\}$

$⇒ \mu = 2 ( \lambda \ne 0 )$

$⇒ \lambda = 4$ $\left\{\text{from equation}\left(i\right)\right\}$

Hence, $\alpha + \beta + \gamma = 14$ and $a + b + c = - 1$

So, $\dfrac{( \alpha + \beta + \gamma{)}^{2}}{( a + b + c{)}^{2}} = 196$

38091.text: Let the mirror image of the point $\left(a, b, c\right)$ with respect to the plane $3x - 4y + 12z + 19 = 0$ be $\left(a - 6, \beta, \gamma\right)$. If $a + b + c = 5$, then $7\beta - 9\gamma$ is equal to  ______.
38091.sol:
Given the mirror image of $P\left(a, b, c\right)$ is ${P}^{'}\left(a - 6, \beta, \gamma\right)$

The mid-point $M = \left(a - 3, \dfrac{\beta + b}{2}, \dfrac{\gamma + c}{2}\right)$

Since $M$ lies on $3x - 4y + 12z + 19 = 0$

$⇒ 3a - 9 - 4\left(\dfrac{\beta + b}{2}\right) + 12\left(\dfrac{\gamma + c}{2}\right) + 19 = 0$

$⇒ 6a - 18 - 4\beta - 4b + 12\gamma + 12c + 38 = 0$

$⇒ 6a - 4b + 12c - 4\beta + 12\gamma + 20 = 0 ⋯ \left(1\right)$

Since $P{P}^{'}$ is parallel to normal of the plane then

$\dfrac{6}{3} = \dfrac{b - \beta}{- 4} = \dfrac{c - \gamma}{12}$

$⇒ b = \beta - 8, c = \gamma + 24$

Given $a + b + c = 5 ⇒ a + \beta - 8 + \gamma + 24 = 5$

$⇒ a = - \beta - \gamma - 11$

Now putting these values in $\left(1\right)$ we get

$6\left(- \beta - \gamma - 11\right) - 4\left(\beta - 8\right) + 12\left(\gamma + 24\right) - 4\beta + 12\gamma + 20 = 0$

$⇒ 7\beta - 9\gamma = 170 - 33 = 137$

42552.text: A radioactive sample decays $\dfrac{7}{8}$ times its original quantity in $15$ minutes. The half-life of the sample is
42552.sol:
Remaining amount of sample is$= 1 - \dfrac{7}{8} = \dfrac{1}{8}$

Using radioactive decay law

$N = {N}_{0}\left(2\right)\dfrac{- t}{{T}_{\dfrac{1}{2}}}$

We have, $\left(2\right)\dfrac{t}{{T}_{\dfrac{1}{2}}} = \dfrac{{N}_{0}}{N} = \dfrac{{N}_{0}}{\dfrac{{N}_{0}}{8}} = 8 = {\left(2\right)}^{3}$

Then, $\dfrac{t}{{T}_{\dfrac{1}{2}}} = 3$

Thus, half life of the sample is $T\dfrac{1}{2} = 5min$.

43953.text: In an adiabatic process, the density of a diatomic gas becomes $32$$n$ times its initial value. The final pressure of the gas is found to be $n$ times the initial pressure. The value of $n$ is:
43953.sol:
Given,

Final density of diatomic gas is ${ρ}_{f} = 32n{ρ}_{i}$

Final pressure is ${P}_{f} = n{P}_{i}$

In adiabatic process, equation of state is given by,

$P{V}^{\gamma} = \text{constant} . . . \left(1\right)$

Where, $V$ is the volume, $P$ is the pressure and $\gamma = \dfrac{7}{5}$ is the ratio of specific heat of diatomic gas

$P{\left(\dfrac{m}{ρ}\right)}^{\gamma} = \text{constant} . . . \left(2\right)$, As $V = \dfrac{m}{ρ}$

and mass is constant, then the pressure is given by

$∴ P ∝ {ρ}^{\gamma}$

$⇒ \dfrac{{P}_{f}}{{P}_{i}} = {\left(\dfrac{{ρ}_{f}}{{ρ}_{i}}\right)}^{\gamma}$

$⇒ \dfrac{n{P}_{i}}{{P}_{i}} = {\left(\dfrac{32{ρ}_{i}}{{ρ}_{i}}\right)}^{{}^{7 / 5}} = ( 32{)}^{7 / 5}$

$∴ n = {2}^{7} = 128$

54461.text: A circular coil of 100 turns has an effective radius of 0.05 m and carries a current of 0.1 A. How much work is required to turn it in an external magnetic field of $1.5 \mathrm{ Wb} / \mathrm{m}^2$ through $180^{{}^{\circ}}$ about its axis perpendicular to the magnetic field? The plane of the coil is initially perpendicular to the magnetic field.
54461.sol:
The potential energy of circular loop in the magnetic field $=-M B \cos \theta$, where $\theta$ is the angle between normal to plane of coil and magnetic field $B$. Initial potential energy, $U_i=-N i A B \cos 0^{{}^{\circ}}=-N i A B$
When coil is turned through $180^{{}^{\circ}}$, therefore final potential energy, $U_f=-N i A B \cos 180^{{}^{\circ}}=N i A B\therefore$ Required work, $W=$ gain in potential energy $=U_f-U_i=N i A B-(-N i A B)=2NiAB$
Here, $N=100, \quad i=0.1 \mathrm{ A}, \quad B=1.5 \mathrm{ Wb} / \mathrm{m}^2$ and radius $r=0.05 \mathrm{ m}\therefore \quad A=\pi r^2=3.14 \times(0.05)^2=7.85 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{ m}^2\therefore$ Work, $\quad W=2 \times 100 \times 0.1 \times 7.85 \times 10^{-3} \times 1.5\Rightarrow \quad W=0.2355 \mathrm{ J}$

55114.subject: Chemistry
55114.text: Propyne on reaction with water in presence of $40\%$ sulphuric acid and $1\%$ mercuric sulphate forms
55114.sol:
Propyne undergoes hydration in the presence of dilute sulphuric acid and mercuric sulphate according to Markovnikov's rule.

The addition of a water molecule to the triple bond initially yields an unstable enol intermediate, prop-1-en-2-ol.

$CH_3-C \equiv CH + H_2O \xrightarrow{Hg^{2+}, H^+} CH_3-C(OH)=CH_2$

The enol intermediate rapidly undergoes tautomerization to form the more stable keto form, propanone.

$CH_3-C(OH)=CH_2 \rightleftharpoons CH_3-CO-CH_3$

Answer: Propanone

58631.subject: Chemistry
58631.text: What is the difference in oxidation number of Mn in $\mathrm{KMnO}_4$ and $\mathrm{MnO}_2$ ?
58631.sol:
The oxidation number of manganese in each compound must be determined to find their difference.

In $\mathrm{KMnO}_4$, potassium has an oxidation state of $+1$ and oxygen is $-2$. For charge neutrality:
$1 \times (+1) + x + 4 \times (-2) = 0$
$x - 7 = 0$
$x = +7$

In $\mathrm{MnO}_2$, oxygen again contributes $-2$ per atom:
$y + 2 \times (-2) = 0$
$y = +4$

The difference in oxidation numbers is $+7 - (+4) = 3$.

The final answer is $\boxed{\text{B}}$

$W = \dfrac{9.84}{24.6}$

$W = 0.4$ g

60558.subject: Mathematics
60558.text: The area (in sq. units) of the region bounded by the curve $y = 2x - x^2$ and the X-axis is...
60558.sol:
The given curve is $y = 2x - x^2$.

To find the points of intersection with the X-axis, set $y = 0$:

$2x - x^2 = 0$

$x(2 - x) = 0 \Rightarrow x = 0, x = 2$

The required area is the integral of the curve from $x = 0$ to $x = 2$:

$A = \int_{0}^{2} (2x - x^2) dx$

$A = \left[ x^2 - \dfrac{x^3}{3} \right]_{0}^{2}$

$A = \left( 2^2 - \dfrac{2^3}{3} \right) - 0$

$A = 4 - \dfrac{8}{3} = \dfrac{4}{3}$ sq. units.

Answer: $\dfrac{4}{3}$

61285.subject: Mathematics
61285.text: $The solution of the differential equation \left(x + 2y^3\right)\dfrac{dy}{dx} - y = 0$ is
options: $x = (c + y^2)y$, where c is the constant of integration
$y = (c + y^2)x$, where c is the constant of integration
$x = (c + y)y$, where c is the constant of integration
$y = (c + x^2)$, where c is the constant of integration
61285.sol:
The given differential equation is $(x + 2y^3)\dfrac{dy}{dx} - y = 0$

Rearranging the terms, we get:

$\dfrac{dx}{dy} = \dfrac{x + 2y^3}{y}$

$\dfrac{dx}{dy} - \dfrac{1}{y}x = 2y^2$

This is a linear differential equation of the form $\dfrac{dx}{dy} + P(y)x = Q(y)$, where $P(y) = -\dfrac{1}{y}$ and $Q(y) = 2y^2$.

The integrating factor (IF) is:

$IF = e^{\int -\dfrac{1}{y} dy} = e^{-\ln y} = \dfrac{1}{y}$

Multiplying the differential equation by the integrating factor and integrating, the solution is given by:

$x \cdot (IF) = \int Q(y) \cdot (IF) dy + c$

$x \left(\dfrac{1}{y}\right) = \int 2y^2 \left(\dfrac{1}{y}\right) dy + c$

$\dfrac{x}{y} = \int 2y dy + c$

$\dfrac{x}{y} = y^2 + c$

$x = y(y^2 + c)$

Answer: $x = (c + y^2)y$, where c is the constant of integration

61294.subject: Mathematics
61294.text: A body cools according to Newton's law of cooling from $100^{}^{\circ}$ C to $60^{}^{\circ}$ C in $20$ minutes. The temperature of the surroundings being $20^{}^{\circ}$ C, then the total time required for the body to cool down to $30^{}^{\circ}$ C is
61294.sol:
According to Newton's law of cooling, the temperature of a body at time $t$ is given by:

$T - T_s = (T_0 - T_s) e^{-kt}$

Given $T_0 = 100^{}^{\circ}$C and $T_s = 20^{}^{\circ}$C. At $t = 20$ minutes, $T = 60^{}^{\circ}$C.

Substituting these values into the equation:

$60 - 20 = (100 - 20) e^{-20k}$

$40 = 80 e^{-20k}$

$e^{-20k} = \dfrac{1}{2}$

Taking the natural logarithm on both sides:

$-20k = -\ln 2 \Rightarrow k = \dfrac{\ln 2}{20}$

Let $t$ be the total time required for the body to cool down to $30^{}^{\circ}$C.

$30 - 20 = (100 - 20) e^{-kt}$

$10 = 80 e^{-kt}$

$e^{-kt} = \dfrac{1}{8} = \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^3$

Taking the natural logarithm again:

$-kt = -3\ln 2 \Rightarrow kt = 3\ln 2$

Substituting the value of $k$:

$\left(\dfrac{\ln 2}{20}\right) t = 3\ln 2$

$t = 60$ minutes.

Answer: $60$ minutes

61355.subject: Mathematics
61355.text: $The sum of the degree and order of the differential equation \sqrt{\frac{\mathrm{d}^2 \mathrm{y}}{\mathrm{d} x^2}}=\sqrt[5]{\frac{\mathrm{dy}}{\mathrm{d} x}-5}$ is
61355.sol:
The differential equation $\sqrt{\frac{\mathrm{d}^2\mathrm{y}}{\mathrm{d} x^2}}=\sqrt[5]{\frac{\mathrm{dy}}{\mathrm{d} x}-5}$ contains fractional powers of derivatives.
Expressing with exponents: $\left(\frac{\mathrm{d}^2\mathrm{y}}{\mathrm{d} x^2}\right)^{1/2} = \left(\frac{\mathrm{dy}}{\mathrm{d} x}-5\right)^{1/5}$.

Raising both sides to the 10th power eliminates the fractional exponents:
$\left[\left(\frac{\mathrm{d}^2\mathrm{y}}{\mathrm{d} x^2}\right)^{1/2}\right]^{10} = \left[\left(\frac{\mathrm{dy}}{\mathrm{d} x}-5\right)^{1/5}\right]^{10}$
which simplifies to $\left(\frac{\mathrm{d}^2\mathrm{y}}{\mathrm{d} x^2}\right)^5 = \left(\frac{\mathrm{dy}}{\mathrm{d} x}-5\right)^2$.

The highest derivative is $\frac{\mathrm{d}^2\mathrm{y}}{\mathrm{d} x^2}$ of second order, establishing order 2.
The highest power of this derivative is 5, giving degree 5.

The sum is therefore $2 + 5 = \boxed{7}$.

63321.text: The measure of the acute angle between the pair of lines $2x^2 + xy - y^2 - x + 2y - 1 = 0$ is:
63321.sol:
Comparing the given equation $2x^2 + xy - y^2 - x + 2y - 1 = 0$ with the general equation $ax^2 + 2hxy + by^2 + 2gx + 2fy + c = 0$, we get:

$a = 2$, $h = \dfrac{1}{2}$, $b = -1$

The acute angle $\theta$ between the pair of lines is given by:

$\tan \theta = \left| \dfrac{2\sqrt{h^2 - ab}}{a + b} \right|$

Substituting the values:

$\tan \theta = \left| \dfrac{2\sqrt{\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^2 - (2)(-1)}}{2 + (-1)} \right|$

$\tan \theta = \left| \dfrac{2\sqrt{\dfrac{1}{4} + 2}}{1} \right| = 2\sqrt{\dfrac{9}{4}} = 3$

Since $\tan \theta = 3$, we can find $\cos \theta$ using the relation $\cos \theta = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{1 + \tan^2 \theta}}$:

$\cos \theta = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{1 + 3^2}} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{10}}$

$\theta = \cos^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{10}}\right)$

Answer: $\cos^{-1}\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{10}}$

63558.subject: Mathematics
63558.text: Two cards are drawn at random from a box which contains 5 cards numbered 1, 1, 2, 2 & 3. If X denotes the sum of the numbers, then the expected value of X is...
63558.sol:
Total number of ways to draw 2 cards from 5 cards is ^{5}C_{2} = 10$.

Let $X$ be the sum of the numbers on the two drawn cards. The possible values of $X$ are 2, 3, 4, 5$.

The probabilities for each sum are:

$P(X = 2) = \dfrac{^{2}C_{2}}{10} = \dfrac{1}{10}$

$P(X = 3) = \dfrac{^{2}C_{1} \times ^{2}C_{1}}{10} = \dfrac{4}{10}$

$P(X = 4) = \dfrac{^{2}C_{1} \times ^{1}C_{1} + ^{2}C_{2}}{10} = \dfrac{3}{10}$

$P(X = 5) = \dfrac{^{2}C_{1} \times ^{1}C_{1}}{10} = \dfrac{2}{10}$

The expected value $E(X)$ is given by $\sum X P(X)$:

$E(X) = 2 \times \dfrac{1}{10} + 3 \times \dfrac{4}{10} + 4 \times \dfrac{3}{10} + 5 \times \dfrac{2}{10}$

$E(X) = \dfrac{2 + 12 + 12 + 10}{10} = \dfrac{36}{10} = 3.6$

Answer: $3.6$

63567.text: Let $F(x)$ be the cumulative distribution function (c.d.f.) of a continuous random variable $X$. If $F(b) = 0.7$ and $P(X > a) = 0.4$, then the value of $P(a < X < b)$ is...
63567.sol:
The cumulative distribution function $F(x)$ is defined as $F(x) = P(X \le x)$.

Given $F(b) = 0.7$, we have $P(X \le b) = 0.7$.

We are also given $P(X > a) = 0.4$.

Since $P(X \le a) + P(X > a) = 1$, we get:

$P(X \le a) = 1 - 0.4 = 0.6$

For a continuous random variable, the probability $P(a < X < b)$ is given by:

$P(a < X < b) = P(X \le b) - P(X \le a)$

Substituting the values:

$P(a < X < b) = 0.7 - 0.6 = 0.1$

Answer: $0.1$

$\sin A + \sin B = 2 \sin\left(\frac{A+B}{2}\right) \cos\left(\frac{A-B}{2}\right) = x$

65631.text: A series LCR circuit is connected to an a.c. source of $230 \mathrm{ V}, 50 \mathrm{ Hz}$. The circuit contains resistance of $80 \Omega$ an inductor having inductive reactance $70 \Omega$ and a capacitor of capacitive reactance $130 \Omega$. The power factor of the circuit is $x$. The value of $x$ is
65631.sol:
The power factor of a series LCR circuit is determined by the ratio of resistance to impedance.

Given resistance $R = 80\ \Omega$, inductive reactance $X_L = 70\ \Omega$, and capacitive reactance $X_C = 130\ \Omega$, the net reactance is $X = X_C - X_L = 60\ \Omega$ since $X_C > X_L$.

The impedance follows as $Z = \sqrt{R^2 + X^2} = \sqrt{80^2 + 60^2} = \sqrt{10000} = 100\ \Omega$.

Thus, the power factor is $\cos \phi = R/Z = 80/100 = 0.8$.

This corresponds to option B, so the answer is $\boxed{\text{B}}$.

Equation of motion for this combined mass is:
$T_1 = (2 + 8)a = 10a$

The tension $T_2$ is responsible for pulling only the block of mass $2\text{ kg}$.

Equation of motion for the $2\text{ kg}$ block is:
$T_2 = 2a$

The ratio of the tensions is:
$\dfrac{T_1}{T_2} = \dfrac{10a}{2a} = \dfrac{5}{1}$

Therefore, $T_1 : T_2 = 5 : 1$.

Answer: $5 : 1$

67551.text: A vehicle is moving with uniform speed along 3 different shaped roads as horizontal, concave and convex. The surface of road on which, the normal reaction on vehicle is maximum is
67551.sol:
The normal reaction on the vehicle is determined by analyzing the forces when moving at uniform speed v on different surfaces.

On a horizontal road, the gravitational force mg is balanced by the normal reaction N_{H}, giving N_{H}=mg.

At the lowest point on a concave road, the centripetal force mv^{2}/r is provided by the normal reaction exceeding gravity: N_{C} − mg=mv^{2}/r, leading to N_{C}=mg + mv^{2}/r.

At the highest point on a convex road, gravity exceeds the normal reaction to provide the centripetal force: mg − N_{X}=mv^{2}/r, so N_{X}=mg − mv^{2}/r.

Comparing the expressions shows N_{C}> N_{H}> N_{X}, indicating the maximum normal reaction occurs on the concave road.

The answer is $\boxed{B}$.

70506.subject: Physics
70506.text:
A vehicle starts from rest and accelerates along straight path at $2 \mathrm{ m} / \mathrm{s}^2$. At the starting point of the vehicle, there is a stationary electric siren. How far has the vehicle nearly gone when the driver hears the siren at $94 \%$ of its value when the vehicle was at rest?
(speed of sound $=330 \mathrm{ m} / \mathrm{s}$ )
70506.sol:
The vehicle's speed when the driver hears the siren at 94% of its original frequency is determined from the Doppler effect for a moving observer receding from a stationary source: $f' = f \left( \frac{v_s - v_o}{v_s} \right).

Given $ f' = 0.94f$ and $v_s = 330\,$\text{m/s}, solve for $ v_o$:

0.94 = \frac{330 - v_o}{330}
$ v_o = 330 - 0.94 $\times330 = 19.8\,\text{m/s}

With constant acceleration $ a = 2\,$\text{m/s}^2$ from rest, the distance traveled to reach this velocity is found from $v^2 = u² + 2ax$:

$19.8^2 = 0 + 2 $\cdot$2 $\cdot$ x$
$392.04 = 4x$
$x = 98.01\,\text{m}

Rounding to the nearest meter gives 98\,\text{m}$, corresponding to option A.

71066.subject: Biology
71066.text: The available biomass for the consumption, to heterotrophs is ----------------.
71066.sol:
Gross primary productivity (GPP) is the total rate of photosynthesis or total biomass produced by primary producers.

A considerable amount of GPP is utilized by plants in respiration (R).

Net primary productivity (NPP) is the gross primary productivity minus respiration losses (NPP = GPP - R).

NPP is the available biomass for the consumption to heterotrophs (herbivores and decomposers).

Answer: Net primary productivity

71635.subject: Chemistry
71635.text: IN a chemical reaction Aniline is treated with $\text{NaNO}_2$ and HCl to form a compound X. When X is further hydrolyzed by supplying heat it forms compound Z. Identify Z in this reaction.
71635.sol:
Aniline ($\text{Ar-NH}_2$) reacts with $\text{NaNO}_2$ and $\text{HCl}$ at $0-5^{{}^{\circ}}\text{C}$ to undergo diazotization, forming benzene diazonium chloride ($\text{Ar-N}_2^+\text{Cl}^-$) as compound X.

$\text{Ar-NH}_2 + \text{NaNO}_2 + 2\text{HCl} \xrightarrow{0-5^{{}^{\circ}}\text{C}} \text{Ar-N}_2^+\text{Cl}^- + \text{NaCl} + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}$

When the diazonium salt X is hydrolyzed by warming with water (supplying heat), it decomposes to form phenol ($\text{Ar-OH}$) as compound Z, along with the evolution of nitrogen gas.

$\text{Ar-N}_2^+\text{Cl}^- + \text{H}_2\text{O} \xrightarrow{\Delta} \text{Ar-OH} + \text{N}_2 + \text{HCl}$

Thus, compound Z is $\text{Ar-OH}$.

Answer: Ar-OH

71839.subject: Chemistry
71839.text:
$\text{H}_3\text{C}-\text{CH}=\text{CH}_2 + \text{H}-\text{Br} \xrightarrow{\large{(\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CO})_2\text{O}_2,\ \text{Benzoyl peroxide}}} \text{H}_3\text{C}-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{Br}$
Which of the following rules is followed when the above reaction occurs?
71839.sol:
The addition of $\text{HBr}$ to an unsymmetrical alkene in the presence of a peroxide (such as benzoyl peroxide) proceeds via a free radical mechanism.

The bromine free radical adds to the less substituted carbon atom of the double bond to generate a more stable secondary free radical intermediate.

This leads to the formation of 1-bromopropane ($\text{H}_3\text{C}-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{Br}$) as the major product.

This regioselectivity is opposite to Markovnikov's rule and is known as the peroxide effect, Kharasch effect, or Anti-Markovnikov's rule.

Answer: Anti-Markovnikovs rule

72466.text:
In Young's double slit experiment using a monochromatic light of wavelength $\lambda$. The path difference (in terms of an integer n) corresponding to any point having one fourth of its peak intensity is
$\{\cos(\pi/3)=1/2,\ \cos(4\pi/3)=-1/2\}$
72466.sol:
The intensity at any point in Young's double slit experiment is given by $I = I_0 \cos^2 \left(\dfrac{\phi}{2}\right)

Given that $ I = $\dfrac{I_0}{4}

\dfrac{I_0}{4} =$ I_0 \cos^2 $\left(\dfrac{\phi}{2}\right)$

$\cos\left(\dfrac{\phi}{2}\right) = \pm \dfrac{1}{2}$

$\dfrac{\phi}{2} = n\pi \pm \dfrac{\pi}{3}$

$\phi = 2n\pi \pm \dfrac{2\pi}{3}$

The phase difference $\phi$ is related to the path difference $\Delta x$ by $\phi = \dfrac{2\pi}{\lambda} \Delta x$

$\dfrac{2\pi}{\lambda} \Delta x = 2\pi \left($ n $\pm \dfrac{1}{3}\right)

\Delta$ x = $\left($ n $\pm \dfrac{1}{3}\right)\lambda

Answer: \left($ n$\pm\dfrac{1}{3}\right)\lambda,$\ n=0,1,2$$

76797.text:
Let $f(x)=|x-1|, g(x)=[x]$ and $h(x)=f(x) g(x)$ where [.] is greatest integer function.
What is $\int_{-1}^0 h(x) d x$ equal to?
76797.sol:
$\begin{array}{ll}
\text{ Given, } & f(x)=|x-1| \qquad ...(i) \\
& g(x)=[x] \qquad ...(ii) \\
and & h(x)=f(x) \cdot g(x) \\
\Rightarrow & h(x)=h(x)-1 \mid \cdot[x] \qquad ...(iii) \\
\end{array} \begin{aligned} \int_{-1}^0 h(x) d x & =\int_{-1}^0 f(x) \cdotg(x) d x \\ & =\int_{-1}^0|x-1| \cdot[x] d x \\ & =\int_{-1}^0(1-x) \cdot(-1) d x \\ & =\int_1^2(x-1) d x=\left[\frac{x^2}{2}-x\right]_1^2 \\ & =\left[0-\left(\frac{1}{2}+1\right)\right]=-\frac{3}{2}\end{aligned}$

77936.subject: Mathematics
77936.text:
Paragraph: Given that $C(n, r): C(n, r+1)=1: 2$ and $C(n, r+1): C(n, r+2)=2: 3$.
Question: What is $r$ equal to?
77936.sol:
$\begin{aligned}
& \frac{{ }^n \mathrm{C}_r}{{ }^n \mathrm{C}_{r+1}}=\frac{1}{2} (given)\\
& \Rightarrow \quad \frac{\frac{n!}{r!(n-r)!}}{\frac{n!}{(r+1)!(n-r-1)!}}=\frac{1}{2} \\
& \Rightarrow \quad \frac{(r+1)!(n-r-1)!}{r!(n-r)!}=\frac{1}{2} \\
& \Rightarrow \frac{(r+1) \cdot r!(n-r-1)!}{r!(n-r)(n-r-1)!}=\frac{1}{2} \\
& \Rightarrow \quad n-r=2(r+1) \\
& \Rightarrow \quad n-r=2 r+2 \\
& \Rightarrow \quad n=3 r+2 ..(i)\\
& \text{ Again, } \\
& \frac{{ }^n C_{r+1}}{{ }^n C_{r+2}}=\frac{2}{3}
\end{aligned}\begin{aligned}
& \Rightarrow \quad \frac{\frac{n!}{(r+1)!(n-r-1)!}}{\frac{n!}{(r+2)!(n-r-2)!}}=\frac{2}{3} \\
& \Rightarrow \quad \frac{(r+2)!(n-r-2)!}{(r+1)!(n-r-1)!}=\frac{2}{3} \\
& \Rightarrow \frac{(r+2)(r+1)!(n-r-2)!}{(r+1)!(n-r-1)(n-r-2)!}=\frac{2}{3} \\
& 2(n-r-1)=3(r+2) \\
& \Rightarrow \quad 2 n-2 r-2=3 r+6 \\
& \Rightarrow \quad 2 n=5 r+8...(ii)
\end{aligned}$
Multiply equation (i) by 2
$2 n=6 r+4$ ...(iii)
From equations (ii) and (iii)
$\begin{aligned}
& & 6 r+4 & =5 r+8 \\
\Rightarrow & & r & =4
\end{aligned}$
Putting the value of $r$ in equation (ii)
$\begin{aligned}
2 n & =5(4)+8 \\
2 n & =20+8 \\
2 n & =28 \\
n & =14 .
\end{aligned}$
Value of $r=4$.

78964.subject: Mathematics
78964.text: In a triangle $ABC$, $\sin A=\cos B+\cos C$ then what is $\tan \left(\dfrac{B}{2}\right)+\cot  \left(\dfrac{B}{2}\right)equal to ?$
78964.sol:
Given $\sin A = \cos B + \cos C$

Using the half-angle and sum-to-product formulas:

$2 \sin\left(\dfrac{A}{2}\right) \cos\left(\dfrac{A}{2}\right) = 2 \cos\left(\dfrac{B+C}{2}\right) \cos\left(\dfrac{B-C}{2}\right)$

In $\Delta ABC$, $A + B + C = \pi$, so $\dfrac{B+C}{2} = \dfrac{\pi}{2} - \dfrac{A}{2}$.

This yields $\cos\left(\dfrac{B+C}{2}\right) = \sin\left(\dfrac{A}{2}\right)$.

Substituting this into the equation:

$2 \sin\left(\dfrac{A}{2}\right) \cos\left(\dfrac{A}{2}\right) = 2 \sin\left(\dfrac{A}{2}\right) \cos\left(\dfrac{B-C}{2}\right)$

Since $A \in (0, \pi)$, $\sin\left(\dfrac{A}{2}\right) \neq 0$. Dividing both sides by $2 \sin\left(\dfrac{A}{2}\right)$:

$\cos\left(\dfrac{A}{2}\right) = \cos\left(\dfrac{B-C}{2}\right)$

Since both $\dfrac{A}{2}$ and $\dfrac{B-C}{2}$ lie in $\left(-\dfrac{\pi}{2}, \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$, we have:

$\dfrac{A}{2} = \pm \dfrac{B-C}{2}$

This implies either $A = B - C$ or $A = C - B$.

If $A = B - C$, then $B = A + C$. Since $A + B + C = \pi$, we get $2B = \pi \Rightarrow B = \dfrac{\pi}{2}$.

If $A = C - B$, then $C = A + B$. Since $A + B + C = \pi$, we get $2C = \pi \Rightarrow C = \dfrac{\pi}{2}$.

Simplifying the required expression:

$\tan\left(\dfrac{B}{2}\right) + \cot\left(\dfrac{B}{2}\right) = \dfrac{\sin\left(\dfrac{B}{2}\right)}{\cos\left(\dfrac{B}{2}\right)} + \dfrac{\cos\left(\dfrac{B}{2}\right)}{\sin\left(\dfrac{B}{2}\right)} = \dfrac{\sin^2\left(\dfrac{B}{2}\right) + \cos^2\left(\dfrac{B}{2}\right)}{\sin\left(\dfrac{B}{2}\right) \cos\left(\dfrac{B}{2}\right)} = \dfrac{2}{\sin B}$

If $B = \dfrac{\pi}{2}$, the value is $\dfrac{2}{\sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)} = 2$.

If $C = \dfrac{\pi}{2}$, then $B \in \left(0, \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$, which means $\sin B < 1$ and $\dfrac{2}{\sin B} > 2$.

Since the given options are constants and the minimum possible value is $2$, the only valid choice among the options is $2$.

Answer: $2$

82585.text: A long solenoid has $1000$ turns. When a current of $4 A$ flows through it the magnetic flux linked with each turn of the solenoid is $4 \times {10}^{- 3}Wb.$ The self-inductance of the solenoid is:
82585.sol:
In the case of self-inductance of the solenoid, magnetic flux $\left(ϕ\right)$ is directly proportional to the current $\left(i\right)$ flowing in the coil. The flux through each turn is equal to the flux linkage.

The relation is given as $Nϕ = Li$, here $N$ is the number of turns and $L$ is inductance.

So putting the given values, we get

$1000 \times 4 \times {10}^{- 3} = L \times 4$

Thus, the self inductance is $1H$.

& =$\left(\frac{200}{100}\right)\left(\frac{20}{40}\right)=$2 $\times \frac{1}{2}=$1 \\

In steady state the amount of heat flowing from one face to the other face in time $t$ is given by $Q=\frac{K A\left(\theta_1-\theta_2\right) t}{l}$ where $K$ is coefficient of thermal conductivity of material of rod $\Rightarrow \quad \frac{\mathrm{Q}}{\mathrm{t}} \propto \frac{\mathrm{A}}{\mathrm{l}} \propto \frac{\mathrm{r}^2}{\mathrm{l}}$
As the metallic rod is melted and the material is formed into a rod of half the radius

$\begin{aligned}\mathrm{V}_{1} & = \mathrm{V}_{2}$ \\
\Rightarrow \quad $\pi \mathrm{r}_{1}^2  \mathrm{l}_{1}$ & =$\pi \mathrm{r}_{2}^2  \mathrm{l}_{2}$ \\
\quad \quad \quad $\mathrm{l} }_{1} &  =\frac{\mathrm{l}_2}{4}
\end{aligned} Now,$ from $Eqs. (i) and (ii)

\begin{aligned}
\Rightarrow \quad & \frac{Q_1}{Q_2}=\frac{r_1^2}{l_1} \times \frac{l_2}{r_2^2}=\frac{r_1^2}{l_1} \times \frac{4 l_1}{\left(r_1 / 2\right)^2} \\
\Rightarrow \quad Q_1 & =16 Q_2
\end{aligned}$

92550.text: A hydrogen atom moving at speed $v$ collides with another hydrogen atom kept at rest. Find the minimum value of $v$ for which one of the atoms may get ionised. The mass of a hydrogen atom $= 1.67 \times {10}^{- 27}kg.$ Assume completely inelastic collision.
92550.sol:
Inelastic collision will take place, if a part of incident kinetic energy is utilised in exciting the atom. Here, one atom is to be ionised, i.e. $∆ E = 13.6eV$

Assuming completely inelastic collision.



For an inelastic collision

${v}_{1} = {v}_{2} = v$

By momentum conservation,

$mv = 2mV$

$⇒ V = \dfrac{v}{2}$

$\dfrac{1}{2}mv^{2} = \dfrac{1}{2} ⋅ 2mV^{2} + ∆ E$

$\begin{cases}= m{\left(\dfrac{v}{2}\right)}^{2} + ∆ E & \left[∵ V = v / 2\right]\end{cases}$

$\dfrac{1}{4}mv^{2} = ∆ E$

$v = \sqrt{\dfrac{4 ∆ E}{m}}$

${v}_\min = \sqrt{\dfrac{4 \times 13.6 \times 1.6 \times {10}^{- 19}}{1.67 \times {10}^{- 27}}}$

$= 7.2 \times {10}^{4}m/s$

or $\text{w} = 6.9 \times {10}^{7} 4{\text{\pi r}^{2}$

or $\text{w} = 6.9 \times {10}^{7} \times 4 \times 3.14 \times {( 3 \times {10}^{- 3} )}^{2}$

93964.sol:
Let ${N}_{0}$ be the initial number of uranium nuclei. After time $t$, let ${N}_{U}$ be the number of uranium nuclei and ${N}_{Pb}$ be the number of lead nuclei.

The number of half-lives passed is

$n = \dfrac{t}{{T}_{half}} = \dfrac{1 . 5 \times {10}^{9}}{4 . 5 \times {10}^{9}} = \dfrac{1}{3}$

${N}_{U} = {N}_{0}{\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)}^{n} = {N}_{0}\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)\dfrac{1}{3}$

${N}_{Pb} = {N}_{0} - {N}_{0}\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)\dfrac{1}{3}$
$\dfrac{{N}_{Pb}}{{N}_{U}} = 2\dfrac{1}{3} - 1 = 0 . 26$

98138.text: Which of the following set of coenzymes are nucleotides of vitamin niacin?
98138.sol: NAD can be synthesized from simple building-blocks (de novo) from the amino acids tryptophan or aspartic acid. In an alternative fashion, more complex components of the coenzymes are taken up from food as the vitamin called niacin. Similar compounds are released by reactions that break down the structure of NAD. These preformed components then pass through a salvage pathway that recycles them back into the active form. Some NAD is also converted into nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide phosphate (NADP).

By conservation of momentum,
Momentum before collision = Momentum after collision

On solving Eqs. (i) and (ii), we get

101383.subject: Physics
101383.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Two satellites of masses $m$ and $4m$ orbiting the Earth in the same circular orbit have the same time period.

Reason (R): The time period of a satellite in a circular orbit is directly proportional to its own mass.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
101383.sol:
The time period of a satellite in a circular orbit of radius $R$ around the Earth (mass $M$) is given by:

$T = 2\pi \sqrt{\dfrac{R^3}{GM}}$

This formula shows that the time period depends only on the mass of the central body ($M$) and the orbital radius ($R$). It is completely independent of the mass of the satellite ($m$).

Therefore, two satellites of different masses ($m$ and $4m$) in the exact same orbit will have the same time period. Thus, Assertion (A) is true.

Since the time period is independent of the satellite's mass, Reason (R) is false.

Answer: (A) is true but (R) is false

101435.text: The change in the gravitational potential energy when a body of mass $m$ is raised to a height $n R$ above the surface of the earth is (here $R$ is the radius of the earth)
101435.sol:
Gravitational potential energ
at any point at a distance $r$ from the centre of earth is
$U=-\frac{G M m}{r}$
At the surface of earth $r=R$,
$\therefore U_s=-\frac{G M m}{R}=-m g R \quad\left(\because g=\frac{G M}{R^2}\right)$
At the height $h=n R$ from the surface of earth $r=R+h=R+n R=R(1+n)$
$\therefore \quad U_h=-\frac{G M m}{R(1+n)}=-\frac{m g R}{(1+n)}$
Change in gravitational potential energy is
$\begin{aligned} \Delta U & =U_h-U_s=-\frac{m g R}{(1+n)}-(-m g R) \\ & =-\frac{m g R}{1+n}+m g R\end{aligned}$
$=m g R\left(1-\frac{1}{1+n}\right)=m g R\left(\frac{n}{1+n}\right)$

So, $\quad T=24 \times 60 \times 60 \mathrm{~s}$
So, angular speed of earth about its own axis
$\omega=\frac{2 \pi}{T}=\frac{2 \pi}{24 \times 60 \times 60} \mathrm{rad} / \mathrm{s}$
At equator, $g^{\prime}=g-R_e \omega^{\prime 2}$

$\Rightarrow \quad \omega^{\prime}=17 \omega$
So, value of $x$ is 17 .

103125.subject: Physics
103125.text: A parallel plate capacitor with plate area $A$ and separation $d$ has an initial capacitance $C_0$ when there is air between the plates. It is then filled with three different dielectric materials. The left half of the space (thickness $d/2$, full area $A$) is filled with a dielectric of constant $K_1 = 2$. The right half of the space (thickness $d/2$) is divided into two equal parts, each of area $A/2$, and filled with dielectrics of constants $K_2 = 3$ and $K_3 = 5$. The new equivalent capacitance of the system is:
103125.sol:
The initial capacitance with air is $C_0 = \dfrac{\varepsilon_0 A}{d}$.

The system can be modeled as a capacitor $C_1$ in series with the parallel combination of capacitors $C_2$ and $C_3$.

For the left half (thickness $d/2$, area $A$):
$C_1 = \dfrac{K_1 \varepsilon_0 A}{d/2} = 2K_1 \left(\dfrac{\varepsilon_0 A}{d}\right) = 2(2)C_0 = 4C_0$.

For the right half, it is split into two equal areas ($A/2$) with thickness $d/2$:
$C_2 = \dfrac{K_2 \varepsilon_0 (A/2)}{d/2} = K_2 \left(\dfrac{\varepsilon_0 A}{d}\right) = 3C_0$.
$C_3 = \dfrac{K_3 \varepsilon_0 (A/2)}{d/2} = K_3 \left(\dfrac{\varepsilon_0 A}{d}\right) = 5C_0$.

$C_2$ and $C_3$ are in parallel, so their equivalent capacitance is:
$C_p = C_2 + C_3 = 3C_0 + 5C_0 = 8C_0$.

Now, $C_1$ is in series with $C_p$. The total equivalent capacitance $C_{eq}$ is:
$C_{eq} = \dfrac{C_1 C_p}{C_1 + C_p} = \dfrac{4C_0 \times 8C_0}{4C_0 + 8C_0} = \dfrac{32C_0}{12} = \dfrac{8}{3}C_0$.

Answer: $\dfrac{8}{3} C_0$

105272.subject: Physics
105272.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): A logic circuit with the Boolean expression $Y = A + \bar{A}B$ is equivalent to an OR gate.

Reason (R): The simplification of the expression $A + \bar{A}B$ to $A + B$ is a direct consequence of De Morgan's laws.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion.
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion.
Assertion is true but Reason is false.
Assertion is false but Reason is true.
105272.sol:
Assertion (A) is true: The Boolean expression $Y = A + \bar{A}B$ can be simplified using the distributive law of Boolean algebra, which states that $A + BC = (A + B)(A + C)$.

Applying this, $A + \bar{A}B = (A + \bar{A})(A + B)$.

Since $A + \bar{A} = 1$, the expression becomes $1 \cdot (A + B) = A + B$.

The expression $Y = A + B$ represents an OR gate. Thus, the logic circuit is equivalent to an OR gate.

Reason (R) is false: The simplification of $A + \bar{A}B$ to $A + B$ relies on the distributive law ($A + BC = (A + B)(A + C)$) and the OR law ($A + \bar{A} = 1$), not De Morgan's laws. De Morgan's laws state that $\overline{A + B} = \bar{A} \cdot \bar{B}$ and $\overline{A \cdot B} = \bar{A} + \bar{B}$.

Answer: Assertion is true but Reason is false.

105565.subject: Physics
105565.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): For a given photosensitive material, if the wavelength of incident light is increased beyond a certain maximum value, photoelectric emission stops.
Reason (R): The work function of a photosensitive material is a characteristic property of the material and is independent of the intensity of incident light.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion and Reason are correct and Reason is the correct explanation for Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are correct but Reason is not the correct explanation for Assertion
Assertion is correct but Reason is incorrect
Assertion is incorrect but Reason is correct
105565.sol:
Assertion (A) is correct: The maximum wavelength that can cause photoelectric emission is called the threshold wavelength. If the incident wavelength exceeds this value, the energy of the incident photons ($E = \dfrac{hc}{\lambda}$) becomes less than the work function of the material, and photoelectric emission stops.

Reason (R) is also correct: The work function is indeed a characteristic property of the given material (depending on its nature and surface impurities) and does not depend on the intensity of the incident light.

However, Reason (R) does not explain Assertion (A). The correct explanation for Assertion (A) is that the energy of a photon is inversely proportional to its wavelength, so increasing the wavelength decreases the photon energy below the required work function.

Therefore, both Assertion and Reason are correct, but Reason is not the correct explanation for Assertion.

Answer: Both Assertion and Reason are correct but Reason is not the correct explanation for Assertion

106442.text: An electron is present in a $4d$ subshell. Which of the following represents the correct set of possible values for its principal ($n$), azimuthal ($l$), and magnetic ($m_l$) quantum numbers?
106442.sol:
For a $4d$ subshell, the principal quantum number $n$ is given by the numerical prefix, so $n = 4$.

The letter '$d$' corresponds to the azimuthal quantum number $l = 2$.

The magnetic quantum number $m_l$ can take integer values from $-l$ to $+l$. For $l = 2$, the possible values of $m_l$ are $-2, -1, 0, +1, +2$.

Therefore, the correct set is $n = 4$, $l = 2$, $m_l = -2, -1, 0, +1, +2$.

Answer: $n = 4$, $l = 2$, $m_l = -2, -1, 0, +1, +2$

108529.subject: Chemistry
108529.text:
Which among the following are true for an irreversible isothermal expansion of an ideal gas?
(i) $W=-Q$
(ii) $\Delta U=0$
(iii) $\Delta H \neq 0$
(iv) $\Delta T=0$
108529.sol:
In case of isothermal irreversible expansion, the gas is allowed to expand slowly, its temperature tends to fall but some of heat from surrounding is conducted to gas, keeping temperature constant $(\Delta T=0)$. Internal energy is directly proportional to $\Delta T$.
$\begin{array}{ll}
\therefore & \Delta U=0, \Delta H=0 \Rightarrow \Delta U=Q+W \\
\therefore & W=-Q
\end{array}$

112652.subject: Chemistry
112652.text: An aromatic compound 'A' with the molecular formula $\text{C}_7\text{H}_7\text{NO}_2$ on reduction with $\text{Sn/HCl}$ gives compound 'B'. Compound 'B' upon treatment with $\text{NaNO}_2\text{/HCl}$ at $273-278\text{ K}$ followed by warming with water gives compound 'C'. Compound 'C' reacts with bromine water to form a tribromo derivative. Identify compound 'A'.
112652.sol:
Compound 'A' ($\text{C}_7\text{H}_7\text{NO}_2$) is a nitrotoluene.

Reduction of nitrotoluene with $\text{Sn/HCl}$ yields a toluidine ('B').

Diazotization of toluidine followed by hydrolysis (warming with water) yields a cresol ('C').

For a cresol to form a tribromo derivative upon reaction with bromine water, all three positions ortho and para to the activating $-\text{OH}$ group must be unsubstituted.

In $m$-cresol (3-methylphenol), the $-\text{CH}_3$ group is at the meta position, leaving both ortho positions and the para position free for electrophilic aromatic substitution. Thus, it forms 2,4,6-tribromo-3-methylphenol.

In contrast, $o$-cresol and $p$-cresol have one of these positions blocked by the methyl group and can only form dibromo derivatives.

Therefore, 'C' is $m$-cresol, 'B' is $m$-toluidine, and 'A' is $m$-nitrotoluene.

Answer: $m$-Nitrotoluene

113891.subject: Chemistry
113891.text:
Assertion A : For a mixture of ethanol and acetone, the enthalpy of mixing ($\Delta_{mix}H$) and volume of mixing ($\Delta_{mix}V$) are both positive.
Reason R : The intermolecular attractive forces between ethanol and acetone are stronger than those between pure ethanol and pure acetone molecules.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below.
options: Both Assertion A and Reason R are correct and Reason R is the correct explanation of Assertion A
Both Assertion A and Reason R are correct but Reason R is NOT the correct explanation of Assertion A
Assertion A is correct but Reason R is not correct
Assertion A is not correct but Reason R is correct
113891.sol:
A mixture of ethanol and acetone shows a positive deviation from Raoult's law. In pure ethanol, the molecules are hydrogen bonded. When acetone is added, its molecules get in between the host molecules and break some of the hydrogen bonds between them.

Because the new intermolecular interactions between ethanol and acetone are weaker than those in the pure components, the solution shows a positive deviation. For such solutions, the enthalpy of mixing ($\Delta_{mix}H$) is positive (endothermic) and the volume of mixing ($\Delta_{mix}V$) is positive (expansion).

Thus, Assertion A is correct because $\Delta_{mix}H$ and $\Delta_{mix}V$ are indeed positive. Reason R is not correct because the interactions between ethanol and acetone are weaker, not stronger.

Answer: Assertion A is correct but Reason R is not correct

114387.subject: Chemistry
114387.text: For strong electrolytes, the plot of molar conductivity ($\Lambda_m$) versus the square root of concentration ($\sqrt{c}$) yields a straight line. If the $y$-intercepts of these plots for $\text{HCl}$, $\text{NaCl}$, and $\text{NaCN}$ are $P$, $Q$, and $R$ respectively, which of the following expressions gives the limiting molar conductivity of $\text{HCN}$?
114387.sol:
According to the Debye-Huckel-Onsager equation, the $y$-intercept of a $\Lambda_m$ versus $\sqrt{c}$ plot represents the limiting molar conductivity ($\Lambda_m^0$) of the electrolyte.

Thus, we are given:
$\Lambda_m^0(\text{HCl}) = P$
$\Lambda_m^0(\text{NaCl}) = Q$
$\Lambda_m^0(\text{NaCN}) = R$

According to Kohlrausch's law of independent migration of ions, the limiting molar conductivity of a weak electrolyte like $\text{HCN}$ can be calculated from strong electrolytes:
$\Lambda_m^0(\text{HCN}) = \lambda^0(\text{H}^+) + \lambda^0(\text{CN}^-)$

By adding and subtracting the limiting molar conductivities of the respective ions, we get:
$\Lambda_m^0(\text{HCN}) = \Lambda_m^0(\text{HCl}) + \Lambda_m^0(\text{NaCN}) - \Lambda_m^0(\text{NaCl})$

Substituting the given values:
$\Lambda_m^0(\text{HCN}) = P + R - Q$

Answer: $P + R - Q$

117780.subject: Chemistry
117780.text: An octahedral complex of $\text{Fe}^{2+}$ has a spin-only magnetic moment of $0$ BM. The Crystal Field Stabilization Energy (CFSE) for this complex, ignoring the pairing energy, is:
117780.sol:
The central metal ion is Fe$^{2+}$, which has an electronic configuration of $[\text{Ar}] 3d^6$.

The spin-only magnetic moment is given as $0$ BM. The formula for magnetic moment is $\mu = \sqrt{n(n+2)}$ BM, where $n$ is the number of unpaired electrons.
Since $\mu = 0$, the number of unpaired electrons $n = 0$.

For an octahedral $d^6$ complex to have zero unpaired electrons, it must be a low-spin complex where all electrons are paired in the lower energy $t_{2g}$ orbitals. The electronic configuration in the crystal field is $t_{2g}^6 e_g^0$.

The Crystal Field Stabilization Energy (CFSE) for an octahedral complex is calculated as:
$\text{CFSE} = (-0.4 n_{t_{2g}} + 0.6 n_{e_g}) \Delta_o$
where $n_{t_{2g}}$ and $n_{e_g}$ are the number of electrons in the $t_{2g}$ and $e_g$ orbitals respectively.

Substituting the values:
$\text{CFSE} = (-0.4 \times 6 + 0.6 \times 0) \Delta_o$
$\text{CFSE} = -2.4 \Delta_o$

A common mistake is assuming a high-spin configuration ($t_{2g}^4 e_g^2$), which would give $-0.4 \Delta_o$, but this contradicts the given magnetic moment of $0$ BM.

Answer: $-2.4 \Delta_o$

118267.subject: Chemistry
118267.text:
Consider the following reactions of 1-bromo-2-methylcyclopentane:
(i) 1-bromo-2-methylcyclopentane $\xrightarrow{\text{aq. KOH, }\Delta}$ A (major)
(ii) 1-bromo-2-methylcyclopentane $\xrightarrow{\text{alc. KOH, }\Delta}$ B (major)

Identify the major products A and B.
118267.sol:
The nature of the solvent plays a crucial role in determining whether an alkyl halide undergoes substitution or elimination with KOH.

In reaction (i), aqueous KOH is used. In an aqueous medium, the hydroxide ion ($\text{OH}^-$) acts primarily as a nucleophile, leading to nucleophilic substitution. The bromine atom in 1-bromo-2-methylcyclopentane is replaced by a hydroxyl group, yielding 2-methylcyclopentanol as the major product A.

In reaction (ii), alcoholic KOH is used. In an alcoholic medium, the alkoxide ions formed act as strong bases, favouring dehydrohalogenation ($\beta$-elimination). The $\beta$-hydrogens are located on C2 (which bears the methyl group) and C5.

According to Zaitsev's rule, elimination occurs predominantly to give the most substituted alkene. Removing the proton from C2 yields 1-methylcyclopentene (a trisubstituted alkene), while removing it from C5 yields 3-methylcyclopentene (a disubstituted alkene). Thus, 1-methylcyclopentene is the major product B.

Option 2 is incorrect because it swaps the functions of aqueous and alcoholic KOH.
Option 3 is incorrect because it identifies the less substituted Hofmann product for the elimination reaction.
Option 4 is incorrect because it assumes a carbocation rearrangement occurs during the substitution step to form a tertiary alcohol.

Answer: A = 2-methylcyclopentanol, B = 1-methylcyclopentene

121348.sol: Commonly known as sac-fungi, the ascomycetes are mostly multicellular, e.g., Penicillium, or rarelyunicellular, e.g., yeast (Saccharomyces). They are saprophytic, decomposers, parasitic or coprophilous (growing on dung). <mark style="background-color: yellow, turquious;">  Mycelium is branched and septate. </mark> The asexual spores are conidia produced exogenously on the special mycelium called conidiophores. Conidia on germination produce mycelium. Sexual spores are called ascosporeswhich are produced endogenously in sac like asci (singular ascus). These asci are arranged in different types of fruiting bodies called ascocarps. Some examples are Aspergillus, Claviceps and Neurospora. Neurospora is used extensively in biochemical and genetic work. Manymembers like morels and truffles are edible and are considered delicacies.

121687.subject: Botany
121687.text: In Numerical Taxonomy, how are the characters processed?
121687.sol: At present phylogenetic classification systems based on evolutionary relationships between the various organisms are acceptable. This assumes that organisms belonging to the same taxa have a common ancestor. We now use information from many other sources too to help resolve difficulties in classification. These become more important when there is no supporting fossil evidence. <mark>Numerical Taxonomy which is now easily carried out using computers is based on all observable characteristics. Numbers and codes are assigned to all the characters and the data are then processed.</mark> In this way each character is given equal importance and at the same time hundreds of characters can be considered. Cytotaxonomy that is based on cytological information like chromosome number, structure, behavior and chemotaxonomy that uses the chemical constituents of the plant to resolve confusions, are also used by taxonomists these days
121687.meta: In Numerical Taxonomy, how are the characters processed?

121747.subject: Botany
121747.text: Which brown alga has a simple branched filamentous form?
121747.sol: The members of phaeophyceae or brown algae are found primarily in marine habitats. They show great variation in size and form. <mark>They range from simple branched, filamentous forms (Ectocarpus)</mark> to profusely branched forms as represented by kelps, which may reach a height of 100 meters. They possess chlorophyll a, c, carotenoids and xanthophylls. They vary in color from olive green to various shades of brown depending upon the amount of the xanthophyll pigment, fucoxanthin present in them. Food is stored as complex carbohydrates, which may be in the form of laminarin or mannitol. The vegetative cells have a cellulosic wall usually covered on the outside by a gelatinous coating of algin. The protoplast contains, in addition to plastids, a centrally located vacuole and nucleus. The plant body is usually attached to the substratum by a holdfast, and has a stalk, the stipe and leaf-like photosynthetic organ – the frond. Vegetative reproduction takes place by fragmentation. Asexual reproduction in most brown algae is by biflagellate zoospores that are pear-shaped and have two unequal laterally attached flagella.

123722.subject: Botany
123722.text: What is the relationship between cell division and reproduction?
options: Cell division is the same as reproduction
Cell division is a part of reproduction
Cell division has no relation with reproduction
Reproduction is the same as cell division
123722.sol: According to the cell theory, cells arise from preexisting cells. The process by which this occurs is called cell division. Any sexually reproducing organism starts its life cycle from a single-celled zygote. Cell division does not stop with the formation of the mature organism but continues throughout its life cycle. The stages through which a cell passes from one division to the next is called the cell cycle. Cell cycle is divided into two phases called (i) Interphase – a period of preparation for cell division, and (ii) Mitosis (M phase) – the actual period of cell division

Rough Endoplasmic Reticulum is primarily involved in protein synthesis. The Golgi apparatus is involved in packaging and secretion, but the actual synthesis of steroidal hormones occurs in the SER. Mitochondria are primarily involved in ATP production.

Answer: Smooth endoplasmic reticulum

124997.subject: Botany
124997.text: Where are the electrons from NADH transferred to after being oxidized by NADH dehydrogenase?
124997.sol: Electrons from NADH produced in the mitochondrial matrix during citric acid cycle are oxidized by an NADH dehydrogenase (complex I), and electrons are then transferred to ubiquinone located within the inner membrane. Ubiquinone also receives reducing equivalents via FADH2 (complex II) that is generated during oxidation of succinate in the citric acid cycle. The reduced ubiquinone (ubiquinol) is then oxidized with the transfer of electrons to cytochrome c via cytochrome bc 1 complex (complex III). Cytochrome c is a small protein attached to the outer surface of the inner membrane and acts as a mobile carrier for transfer of electrons between complex III and IV. Complex IV refers to cytochrome c oxidase complex containing cytochromes a and a3 , and two copper centres.

125313.subject: Botany
125313.text: What did Ingenhousz observe with an aquatic plant in bright sunlight?

125313.sol: Can you imagine how Priestley would have conducted the experiment using a candle and a plant? Remember, he would need to rekindle the candle to test whether it burns after a few days. How many different ways can you think of to light the candle without disturbing the set-up?Using a similar setup as the one used by Priestley, but by placing it once in the dark and once in the sunlight, Jan Ingenhousz (1730-1799) showed that sunlight is essential to the plant process that somehow purifies the air fouled by burning candles or breathing animals. Ingenhousz in an elegant experiment with an aquatic plant showed that in bright sunlight, small bubbles were formed around the green parts while in the dark they did not. Later he identified these bubbles to be of oxygen. Hence he showed that it is only the green part of the plants that could release oxygen.

128673.text: Gigantism and acromegaly are due to
128673.sol:
The anterior pituitary secretes growth hormone. Often, it is known as somatotropin. Growth hormone hypersecretion produces gigantism in children and acromegaly in adults. A tumor in the thyroid is responsible for the hypersecretion of growth hormone in the pituitary gland (hyperpituitarism).

128742.subject: Zoology
128742.text: Which of the following is the largest gland in an adult man ?
128742.sol: Liver is endodermal in origin and is the largest gland in human body. It is the busiest and largest chemical factory in the body.Liver cells secrete bile directly into bile capillaries, which is used in the emulsification and absorption of fats. Besides, it also functions in manufacture of anticoagulant heparin, plasma protein like albumin, fibrinogen and prothrombin and in deamination of proteins.Thyroid gland (measures 3-7 cm in length and 25 gm in weight in adults) a median endocrine gland located below larynx is the largest endocrine gland in the body. Thyroxine $\left(\mathrm{T}_4\right)$, produced by thyroid gland, function mainly in controlling metabolism, ie, basal metabolic rate of the body.Pancreas is a mixed gland (heterocrine gland) with both exocrine and endocrine portions. The average length of pancreas is $12-15 \mathrm{~cm}$ and weight is $50-70 \mathrm{gm}$. Insulin, glucagon, somatostatin are the hormones secreted by different cells of endocrine portion of pancreas.Thymus gland (at birth weights 10-12 gm, at puberty $20-30 \mathrm{gm}$ and at old age it weighs 3-6 gm ) is mainly concerned with immunological functions but becomes inconspicuous after puberty.

128862.subject: Zoology
128862.text: What is the fibrous tissue called that separates the atrium and ventricle of the same side in the human heart?
128862.sol: Our heart has four chambers, two relatively small upper chambers called atria and two larger lower chambers called ventricles. A thin, muscular wall called the interatrial septum separates the right and the left atria, whereas a thick-walled, the inter-ventricular septum, separates the left and the right ventricles. The atrium and the ventricle of the same side are also separated by a thick fibrous tissue called the atrio-ventricular septum. However, each of these septa are provided with an opening through which the two chambers of the same side are connected. The opening between the right atrium and the right ventricle is guarded by a valve formed of three muscular flaps or cusps, the tricuspid valve, whereas a bicuspid or mitral valve guards the opening between the left atrium and the left ventricle
