129521.subject: Zoology
129521.text: What is the process by which nearly 99% of the filtrate is reabsorbed by the renal tubules?
129521.sol: A comparison of the volume of the filtrate formed per day (180 litres per day) with that of the urine released (1.5 litres), suggest that nearly 99 per cent of the filtrate has to be reabsorbed by the renal tubules. This process is called reabsorption. The tubular epithelial cells in different segments of nephron perform this either by active or passive mechanisms. For example, substances like glucose, amino acids, Na+, etc., in the filtrate are reabsorbed actively whereas the nitrogenous wastes are absorbed by passive transport. Reabsorption of water also occurs passively in the initial segments of the nephron.

129553.subject: Zoology
129553.text: What is the role of Angiotensin II in the Renin-Angiotensin mechanism?
129553.sol: The JGA plays a complex regulatory role. A fall in glomerular blood flow/glomerular blood pressure/GFR can activate the JG cells to release renin which converts angiotensinogen in blood to angiotensin I and further to angiotensin II. Angiotensin II, being a powerful vasoconstrictor, increases the glomerular blood pressure and thereby GFR. Angiotensin II also activates the adrenal cortex to release Aldosterone. Aldosterone causes reabsorption of Na+ and water from the distal parts of the tubule. This also leads to an increase in blood pressure and GFR. This complex mechanism is generally known as the Renin-Angiotensin mechanism.

129786.subject: Zoology
129786.text: What type of respiratory structures are used by most aquatic arthropods and molluscs?
129786.sol: . Lower invertebrates like sponges, coelenterates, flatworms, etc., exchange O2 with CO2 by simple diffusion over their entire body surface. Earthworms use their moist cuticle and insects have a network of tubes (tracheal tubes) to transport atmospheric air within the body. Special vascularized structures called gills (branchial respiration) are used by most of the aquatic arthropods and molluscs whereas vascularised bags called lungs (pulmonary respiration) are used by the terrestrial forms for the exchange of gases. Among vertebrates, fishes use gills whereas amphibians, reptiles, birds and mammals respire through lungs. Amphibians like frogs can respire through their moist skin (cutaneous respiration) also.

130618.sol: A discussion on Reproductive Health is incomplete without a mention of infertility. A large number of couples all over the world including India are infertile, i.e., they are unable to produce children inspite of unprotected sexual co-habitation. The reasons for this could be many–physical, congenital, diseases, drugs, immunological or even psychological. In India, often the female is blamed for the couple being childless, but more often than not, the problem lies in the male partner. Specialised health care units (infertility clinics, etc.) could help in diagnosis and corrective treatment of some of these disorders and enable these couples to have children. However, where such corrections are not possible, the couples could be assisted to have children through certain special techniques commonly known as assisted reproductive technologies (ART).

131523.text: What is the role of RNA polymerase in transcription?
options: It facilitates opening of the helix
It catalyzes transcription of all types of RNA

131523.sol: In bacteria, there are three major types of RNAs: mRNA (messenger RNA), tRNA (transfer RNA), and rRNA (ribosomal RNA). All three RNAs are needed to synthesize a protein in a cell. The mRNA provides the template, tRNA brings aminoacids and reads the genetic code, and rRNAs play structural and catalytic roles during translation. There is single DNA-dependent RNA polymerase that catalyzes transcription of all types of RNA in bacteria. RNA polymerase binds to promoter and initiates transcription (Initiation)

131614.subject: Zoology
131614.text: When is a DNA mutation referred to as a DNA polymorphism?
options: When the mutation is not inheritable
When the mutation occurs in coding DNA sequence
When more than one variant at a locus occurs in a population with a frequency greater than 0.01
When the mutation occurs in non-coding DNA sequence
131614.sol: As polymorphism in DNA sequence is the basis of genetic mapping of human genome as well as of DNA fingerprinting, it is essential that we understand what DNA polymorphism means in simple terms. Polymorphism (variation at genetic level) arises due to mutations. New mutations may arise in an individual either in somatic cells or in the germ cells (cells that generate gametes in sexually reproducing organisms). If a germ cell mutation does not seriously impair an individual's ability to have offspring who can transmit the mutation, it can spread to the other members of the population (through sexual reproduction). Allelic sequence variation has traditionally been described as a DNA polymorphism if more than one variant (allele) at a locus occurs in the human population with a frequency greater than 0.01.

132219.subject: Zoology
132219.text: How did Henking’s observations contribute to the understanding of sex determination?
options: He discovered the role of mitochondria in sex determination
He observed that the X body was actually a chromosome
He found that X bodies were responsible for mutation
He proved that sex determination was environmental
132219.sol: Henking (1891) could trace a specific nuclear structure all through spermatogenesis in a few insects, and it was also observed by him that 50 per cent of the sperm received this structure after spermatogenesis, whereas the other 50 per cent sperm did not receive it. Henking gave a name to this structure as the X body but he could not explain its significance. Further investigations by other scientists led to the conclusion that the ‘X body’ of Henking was in fact a chromosome and that is why it was given the name X-chromosome.

132455.subject: Zoology
132455.text: Select the incorrect statement with respect to the mechanism of sex determination in birds.
options: It represents a mechanism of female heterogamety.
The total number of chromosomes is the same in both males and females.
Females produce two different types of ova in terms of sex chromosomes.
Males produce two different types of sperms, half with a Z chromosome and half with a W chromosome.
132455.sol:
In birds, the mechanism of sex determination is of the ZZ-ZW type.

Females are heterogametic (ZW) and produce two different types of ova: 50% carrying a Z chromosome and 50% carrying a W chromosome.

Males are homogametic (ZZ) and produce only one type of sperm, all of which carry a Z chromosome. Therefore, the statement that males produce two different types of sperms is incorrect.

Both males and females have the same total number of chromosomes, as they both possess an equal number of autosomes and two sex chromosomes.

Answer: Males produce two different types of sperms, half with a Z chromosome and half with a W chromosome.

options: improving the quality of human race by symptomatic treatment of genetic diseases.
improving the quality of human populations by the application of genetic principles.
improving the quality of human race by providing best suitable environment.
132558.sol: Eugenics is the study of methods of improving the quality of human populations by the application of genetic principles. Positive eugenics would seek to do this by selective breeding programmes. Negative eugenics aims to eliminate harmful genes (e.g., those causing haemophilia and colour blindness) by counselling any prospective parents who are likely to be carriers.

132650.subject: Zoology
132650.text: What does observing stars on a clear night sky allow us to do?
options: Observe objects in our immediate surroundings
See objects that are currently emitting light
132650.sol: Evolutionary Biology is the study of history of life forms on earth. What exactly is evolution? To understand the changes in flora and fauna that have occurred over millions of years on earth, we must have an understanding of the context of origin of life, i.e., evolution of earth, of stars and indeed of the universe itself. Understanding the evolution of earth, stars, and the universe is essential for comprehending the changes in flora and fauna over time.The origin of life and evolution of life forms is referred to as the longest of all construed and conjectured stories. When we look at stars on a clear night sky we are, in a way, looking back in time. Stellar distances are measured in light years. What we see today is an object whose emitted light started its journey millions of year back and from trillions of kilometres away and reaching our eyes now. However, when we see objects in our immediate surroundings we see them instantly and hence in the present time. Therefore, when we see stars we apparently are peeping into the past.

133297.text: What is a common approach for the treatment of cancer?
133297.sol: Biopsy is a procedure where a piece of the suspected tissue is cut into thin sections and is stained and examined under a microscope (histopathological studies) by a pathologist.Early detection of cancers is essential as it allows the disease to be treated successfully in many cases.Antibodies against cancer-specific antigens are used for the detection of certain cancers. Identification of genes in individuals with inherited susceptibility to certain cancers may be very helpful in the prevention of cancers. Such individuals may be advised to avoid exposure to particular carcinogens to which they are susceptible.The common approaches for treatment of cancer are surgery, radiation therapy, and immunotherapy.Majority of chemotherapy drugs have side effects like hair loss, anaemia, decreased appetite, etc.Tumor cells avoid detection and destruction by the immune system, so patients are given substances like biological response modifiers, such as α-interferon, to activate their immune system and help destroy the tumor.S

133724.subject: Zoology
133724.text: Who was awarded the Nobel Prize for the discovery of penicillin?
133724.sol: Alexander Fleming while working on Staphylococci bacteria, once observed a mould growing in one of his unwashed culture plates around which Staphylococci could not grow. He found out that it was due to a chemical produced by the mould and he named it Penicillin after the mould Penicillium notatum. However, its full potential as an effective antibiotic was established much later by Ernest Chain and Howard Florey. This antibiotic was extensively used to treat American soldiers wounded in World War II. Fleming, Chain and Florey were awarded the Nobel Prize in 1945, for this discovery.

135351.text: A bacterial population is cultured in a laboratory flask provided with unlimited nutrients and space. Which of the following correctly describes the expected growth curve shape, the resource condition, and the governing mathematical equation for this population?
options: J-shaped curve, unlimited resources, $N_t = N_0 e^{rt}$
S-shaped curve, limited resources, $N_t = N_0 e^{rt}$
135351.sol:
When resources in a habitat are unlimited, each species has the ability to realize fully its innate potential to grow in number. This results in exponential or geometric growth, which yields a J-shaped growth curve when population density is plotted against time.

The mathematical representation of this exponential growth in its integral form is $N_t = N_0 e^{rt}$.

The S-shaped (sigmoid) curve and the logistic growth equation $\dfrac{dN}{dt} = rN\left(\dfrac{K-N}{K}\right)$ apply to populations growing under limited resource conditions.

Answer: J-shaped curve, unlimited resources, $N_t = N_0 e^{rt}$

301668.text: In a test, an examinee either guesses or copies or knows the answer to a multiple choice question with four choices. The probability that he makes a guess is $\dfrac{1}{3}$ and the probability that he copies the answer is $\dfrac{1}{6}$. The probability that his answer is correct given that he copies it is $\dfrac{1}{8}$. The probability that his answer is correct, given that he guesses it is $\dfrac{1}{4}$. The probability that he knew the answer to the question given that he correctly answered, is
301668.sol:
Let ${E}_{1}, {E}_{2}$ and ${E}_{3}$ are the events that the examinee guesses, copies and knows the answer and $E$ is the event that he answers correctly.

Then, $\text{P} \left({E}_{1}\right) = \dfrac{1}{3} \text{,} \text{P} \left({E}_{2}\right) = \dfrac{1}{6}$

and $\text{P} \left({E}_{3}\right) = 1 - \left(\dfrac{1}{3} + \dfrac{1}{6}\right) = \dfrac{1}{2}$

∴ Required probability = $\text{P} \left(\dfrac{{E}_{3}}{\text{E}}\right)

$= $\dfrac{\text{P} \left(\dfrac{\text{E}}{{E}_{3}}\right) \cdot \text{P} \left({E}_{3}\right)}{\text{P} \left(\dfrac{\text{E}}{{E}_{1}}\right) \cdot \text{P} \left({E}_{1}\right) + \text{P} \left(\dfrac{\text{E}}{{E}_{2}}\right) \cdot \text{P} \left({E}_{2}\right) + \text{P} \left(\dfrac{\text{E}}{{E}_{3}}\right) \cdot \text{P} \left({E}_{3}\right)}

$= \dfrac{1 \times \dfrac{1}{2}}{\left(\dfrac{1}{4} \times \dfrac{1}{3}\right) + \left(\dfrac{1}{8} \times \dfrac{1}{6}\right) + \left(1 \times \dfrac{1}{2}\right)} = \dfrac{2 4}{2 9}

303144.chapter: Centre of Mass, Linear momentum, Collision
303144.text: A circular disc of diameter $d$ and a square plate of edge $d$ are placed touching each other at the midpoint of an edge of the plate, as shown in the figure. Determine the centre of mass of the combination, assuming the same mass per unit area for both plates.
options: $\dfrac{4d}{4 + \pi}$ to the right of the centre of the disc
$\dfrac{2d}{4 + \pi}$ to the right of the centre of the disc
$\dfrac{d}{1 + \pi}$ to the right of the centre of the disc
$\dfrac{\pi d}{4 + \pi}$ to the right of the centre of the disc
303144.sol:
Let the centre of the circular disc be the origin $(0, 0)$.

Let $\sigma$ be the mass per unit area of both plates.

The mass of the circular disc is $m_1 = \sigma \pi \left(\dfrac{d}{2}\right)^2 = \dfrac{\sigma \pi d^2}{4}$.
The centre of mass of the disc is at $x_1 = 0$.

The mass of the square plate is $m_2 = \sigma d^2$.
Since the square plate touches the disc at the midpoint of its edge, the distance from the centre of the disc to the centre of the square plate is the sum of the radius of the disc and half the edge length of the square. Thus, the centre of mass of the square plate is at $x_2 = \dfrac{d}{2} + \dfrac{d}{2} = d$.

The position of the centre of mass of the combination is given by:

$x_{cm} = \dfrac{m_1 x_1 + m_2 x_2}{m_1 + m_2}$

Substituting the values, we get:

$x_{cm} = \dfrac{\left(\dfrac{\sigma \pi d^2}{4}\right)(0) + (\sigma d^2)(d)}{\dfrac{\sigma \pi d^2}{4} + \sigma d^2}$

$x_{cm} = \dfrac{\sigma d^3}{\sigma d^2 \left(\dfrac{\pi}{4} + 1\right)}$

$x_{cm} = \dfrac{d}{\dfrac{\pi + 4}{4}} = \dfrac{4d}{4 + \pi}$

Therefore, the centre of mass of the combination is at a distance of $\dfrac{4d}{4 + \pi}$ to the right of the centre of the disc.

303573.subject: Physics
303573.text: At a certain confluence, river Yamuna mixes with the river Chambal and becomes river Kaveri. Suppose Yamuna has a width of $12 \text{ m}$, Chambal has a width of $8 \text{ m}$ and Kaveri has a width of $16 \text{ m}$. Assume that the depth of water is identical in all three rivers. If the average speed of water in Yamuna is $20 \text{ km h}^{-1}$ and in Chambal is $16 \text{ km h}^{-1}$, determine the average speed of water in the river Kaveri.
303573.sol:
According to the equation of continuity, the total volume flow rate of water before the confluence is equal to the volume flow rate after the confluence.

$Q_{Kaveri} = Q_{Yamuna} + Q_{Chambal}$

$A_K v_K = A_Y v_Y + A_C v_C$

Since the depth $d$ is identical in all three rivers, the cross-sectional area is given by $A = w \times d$, where $w$ is the width.

$w_K d v_K = w_Y d v_Y + w_C d v_C$

Dividing by $d$ gives:

$w_K v_K = w_Y v_Y + w_C v_C$

Substituting the given values:

$16 \times v_K = 12 \times 20 + 8 \times 16$

$16 v_K = 240 + 128$

$16 v_K = 368$

303726.text: Determine the radius of the circular orbit for a satellite travelling with an angular speed equal to the angular speed of the earth's rotation. The mass of the earth is $6 \times 10^{24} \text{ kg}$.
303726.sol:
The angular speed of the earth's rotation is $\omega = \dfrac{2\pi}{T}$, where $T = 24 \text{ hours} = 86400 \text{ s}$.

For a satellite in a circular orbit, the gravitational force provides the necessary centripetal force:

$\dfrac{GMm}{r^2} = m\omega^2 r$

$r^3 = \dfrac{GM}{\omega^2} = \dfrac{GMT^2}{4\pi^2}$

Substituting the given values $M = 6 \times 10^{24} \text{ kg}$, $G = 6.67 \times 10^{-11} \text{ N m}^2 \text{ kg}^{-2}$, and $T = 86400 \text{ s}$:

$r^3 = \dfrac{6.67 \times 10^{-11} \times 6 \times 10^{24} \times (86400)^2}{4\pi^2}$

$r^3 \approx \dfrac{40.02 \times 10^{13} \times 7.465 \times 10^9}{39.48}$

$r^3 \approx 75.67 \times 10^{21} \text{ m}^3$

Taking the cube root:

$r \approx 4.23 \times 10^7 \text{ m} = 42300 \text{ km}$

303902.subject: Physics
303902.text: A diver with a moment of inertia of $6.0 \text{ kg-m}^2$ about an axis passing through his centre of mass rotates about this axis at an angular speed of $2 \text{ rad/s}$. If the diver folds his hands and feet, reducing the moment of inertia to $5.0 \text{ kg-m}^2$, what will be the new angular speed?
303902.sol:
According to the principle of conservation of angular momentum, if no external torque acts on a system, its total angular momentum remains constant.

Initial angular momentum $L_1 = I_1 \omega_1$

Final angular momentum $L_2 = I_2 \omega_2$

Equating the initial and final angular momentum:

$I_1 \omega_1 = I_2 \omega_2$

Substituting the given values:

$6.0 \times 2 = 5.0 \times \omega_2$

$\omega_2 = \dfrac{12.0}{5.0} = 2.4 \text{ rad/s}$

304210.subject: Physics
304210.chapter: Wave Motion and Waves on a String
304210.text: A wave travels on a string in the positive $x$-direction at a velocity $v$. The shape of the string at $t = t_0$ is described by $g(x, t_0) = A \sin(x/a)$. Determine the wave equation for a general time $t$.
304210.sol:
The general equation of a wave traveling in the positive $x$-direction with velocity $v$ is given by $f(x, t) = h(x - vt)$.

At $t = t_0$, the wave equation is given as $f(x, t_0) = h(x - vt_0) = A \sin \left(\dfrac{x}{a}\right).

Let $z = x - vt_0$, which implies $x = z + vt_0$.

Substituting this into the function gives $h(z) = A \sin \left(\dfrac{z + vt_0}{a}\right)$.

For a general time $t$, replace $z$ with $x - vt$:

$f(x, t) = h(x - vt) = A \sin \left(\dfrac{x - vt + vt_0}{a}\right)$

$f(x, t) = A \sin \$left(\dfrac{x - v(t - t_0)}{a}\right)

305119.subject: Physics
305119.text: Evaluate the potential difference $V_a - V_b$ between points $a$ and $b$ for the circuit designated as (d) in the figure.
305119.sol:
In the circuit labeled (d), let the potential at node $a$ be $V_a = 0$.

The circuit consists of three parallel branches connected between nodes $a$ and $b$. Each branch contains a battery and a capacitor in series.

For all three batteries, the positive terminal (longer line) is oriented towards the right.

The potentials at the intermediate nodes between the batteries and capacitors are $6 \text{ V}$ (top branch), $12 \text{ V}$ (middle branch), and $24 \text{ V}$ (bottom branch).

Applying the principle of charge conservation for the isolated plates connected to node $b$:

$4(V_b - 6) + 2(V_b - 12) + 1(V_b - 24) = 0$

Expanding the equation gives $4V_b - 24 + 2V_b - 24 + V_b - 24 = 0$.

$7V_b - 72 = 0 \implies V_b = \dfrac{72}{7} \approx 10.28 \text{ V}$.

The potential difference is $V_a - V_b = 0 - 10.28 = -10.28 \text{ V}$, which corresponds to $-10.3 \text{ V}$.

305260.subject: Physics
305260.text: An ammeter needs to be built to measure currents up to $2.0\text{ A}$. If the coil has a resistance of $25\Omega$ and requires $1\text{ mA}$ for full-scale deflection, determine the required resistance of the shunt.
305260.sol:
Given, maximum current to be measured, $I = 2.0\text{ A}$

Resistance of the galvanometer coil, $R_g = 25\Omega$

Current for full-scale deflection, $I_g = 1\text{ mA} = 10^{-3}\text{ A}$

The shunt resistance $S$ required is given by the formula:

$S = \dfrac{I_g R_g}{I - I_g}$

Since $I_g$ is very small compared to $I$, we can approximate $I - I_g \approx I$

$S \approx \dfrac{I_g R_g}{I}$

$S = \dfrac{10^{-3} \times 25}{2.0}$

$S = 12.5 \times 10^{-3}\Omega$

$S = 0.0125\Omega$

305980.chapter: Magnetic Field due to a Current
305980.text: A long, thin, hollow cylindrical tube of radius $r$ carries a current $i$ along its length. Calculate the magnitude of the magnetic field at a distance $r/2$ from the surface, outside the tube.
305980.sol:
Let the distance of the point from the axis of the cylinder be $R$.

Since the point is at a distance $r/2$ from the surface outside the tube, we have $R = r + \dfrac{r}{2} = \dfrac{3r}{2}$.

By Ampere's circuital law, the magnetic field outside a long cylindrical tube carrying current $i$ is given by:

$\oint \vec{B} \cdot d\vec{l} = \mu_0 i$

$B(2\pi R) = \mu_0 i$

$B = \dfrac{\mu_0 i}{2\pi R}$

Substituting $R = \dfrac{3r}{2}$:

$B = \dfrac{\mu_0 i}{2\pi \left(\dfrac{3r}{2}\right)} = \dfrac{\mu_0 i}{3\pi r}$

During a specific thermal collision, a valence electron gains an energy equal to $2kT$, just reaching one of the acceptor levels. Assuming the initial energy of the electron was at the top edge of the valence band and the temperature $T$ is $300 \text{ K}$, determine the energy of the acceptor levels above the valence band.
306092.sol:
The energy required for the electron to reach the acceptor level from the top of the valence band is given as $\Delta E = 2kT$.

Substituting the value of the Boltzmann constant $k = 8.62 \times 10^{-5} \text{ eV/K}$ and temperature $T = 300 \text{ K}$:

306109.subject: Physics
306109.text: A potential barrier of $250 \text{ meV}$ exists across a $p$-$n$ junction. A hole possessing a kinetic energy of $300 \text{ meV}$ approaches the junction from the $p$-side. Determine the kinetic energy of the hole after it crosses the junction.
306109.sol:
The potential barrier across a $p$-$n$ junction opposes the motion of majority charge carriers. The electric field in the depletion region is directed from the $n$-side to the $p$-side.

When a hole (which acts as a positive charge) moves from the $p$-side to the $n$-side, it moves against the electric field and loses kinetic energy equal to the potential barrier energy.

By conservation of energy, the final kinetic energy $K_{f}$ of the hole after crossing the junction is given by:

$K_{f} = K_{i} - e V_{0}$

where $K_{i}$ is the initial kinetic energy and $e V_{0}$ is the potential barrier energy.

Substituting the given values:

$K_{f} = 300 \text{ meV} - 250 \text{ meV} = 50 \text{ meV}$

306319.subject: Physics
306319.text: Through what potential difference must an electron be accelerated to give it a speed of $0.9c$?
306319.sol:
The speed of the electron is $v = 0.9c$, which is comparable to the speed of light, so relativistic mechanics must be used.

The relativistic factor $\gamma$ is given by:
$\gamma = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{1 - \dfrac{v^2}{c^2}}} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{1 - 0.81}} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{0.19}} \approx 2.294$

The kinetic energy $K$ of the electron is:
$K = (\gamma - 1)m_0 c^2$

Using the rest mass energy of an electron, $m_0 c^2 \approx 0.511 \text{ MeV}$:
$K = (2.294 - 1) \times 0.511 \text{ MeV} = 1.294 \times 0.511 \text{ MeV} \approx 0.661 \text{ MeV} = 661 \text{ keV}$

Since the kinetic energy is gained by accelerating the electron through a potential difference $V$, we have $K = eV$.

$V = \dfrac{661 \text{ keV}}{e} = 661 \text{ kV}$

306517.subject: Physics
306517.text: The pressure of an ideal gas is given by the expression $p = \dfrac{2E}{3V}$. In this formula, $E$ denotes the
306517.sol:
The pressure of an ideal gas according to the kinetic theory of gases is given by $p = \dfrac{1}{3} \rho v_{rms}^2$

Since density $\rho = \dfrac{M}{V}$, where $M$ is the total mass of the gas and $V$ is the volume, we get $p = \dfrac{1}{3} \dfrac{M}{V} v_{rms}^2$

The translational kinetic energy of the gas molecules is given by $E = \dfrac{1}{2} M v_{rms}^2$

From this, we can write $M v_{rms}^2 = 2E$

Substituting this into the expression for pressure, we obtain $p = \dfrac{1}{3V} (2E) = \dfrac{2E}{3V}$

Thus, $E$ represents the translational kinetic energy of the ideal gas.

306797.subject: Physics
306797.text: During a photoelectric effect experiment, the collector plate is maintained vertically above the emitter plate. A light source is turned on, and a saturation photocurrent is measured. Following this, a vertically downward electric field is switched on.
options: The kinetic energy of the electrons will increase.
306797.sol:
The collector plate is placed vertically above the emitter plate, so the emitted photoelectrons travel in the upward direction.

When a vertically downward electric field $\vec{E}$ is switched on, the force experienced by an electron of charge $-e$ is $\vec{F} = -e\vec{E}$. Since the electric field is directed downwards, the force on the electrons will be directed upwards.

This upward force acts in the direction of motion of the electrons, causing them to accelerate. As a result, the kinetic energy of the electrons will increase as they move towards the collector plate.

The saturation photocurrent depends only on the intensity of the incident light and the number of photoelectrons emitted per second, so it remains unchanged.

The threshold wavelength is a characteristic property of the emitter material (its work function) and is unaffected by the external electric field.

Because the electrons acquire additional kinetic energy from the electric field, a greater retarding potential would be required to stop them, meaning the magnitude of the stopping potential will increase, not decrease.

309094.subject: Chemistry
309094.text: Identify the major product $\mathrm{X}$ in the following reaction sequence:
309094.sol:
The given reaction is the hydroboration-oxidation of 1-methylcyclohexene.

The reagents $\text{B}_2\text{H}_6$ followed by $\text{H}_2\text{O}_2$ in an alkaline medium ($\text{OH}^-$) cause the anti-Markovnikov addition of water ($\text{H}$ and $\text{OH}$) across the carbon-carbon double bond.

In 1-methylcyclohexene, the double bond is between C1 (which bears the methyl group) and C2. According to anti-Markovnikov regioselectivity, the $\text{OH}$ group attaches to the less substituted carbon, which is C2, while the $\text{H}$ atom attaches to the more substituted carbon, C1. This forms 2-methylcyclohexanol.

Hydroboration-oxidation proceeds via a syn-addition mechanism, meaning the $\text{H}$ and $\text{OH}$ groups add to the same face of the double bond.

If $\text{H}$ and $\text{OH}$ add from the bottom face of the ring, the added $\text{H}$ at C1 will be pointing down, pushing the existing $\text{CH}_3$ group up. The added $\text{OH}$ at C2 will also be pointing down. This results in the $\text{CH}_3$ group (up) and the $\text{OH}$ group (down) being on opposite sides of the ring, forming trans-2-methylcyclohexanol.

Evaluating the given structures, the image corresponding to option (C) correctly shows the $\text{CH}_3$ group pointing up at C1 and the $\text{OH}$ group pointing down at C2, which represents the trans-2-methylcyclohexanol product.

310503.text: A tennis ball is dropped on a horizontal smooth surface. It bounces back to its original position after hitting the surface. Which one of the following sketches describes the variation of its kinetic energy $K$ with $t$time most appropriately? The figures are only illustrative and not to the scale.
310503.sol:
When ball of mass $' m '$ dropped from height and strikes to ground.It's kinetic energy is converting into elastic potential energy due to compression.

So after time $' t '$ its final velocity,

$v = u + at$

$u$ is initial velocity of ball, $a$ is acceleration of ball and $t$ is time.

$⇒ v = 0 + \left(- g\right)t$

$v = - gt$

Negative sign shows downward direction.

Now kinetic energy of ball,

$K . E . = \dfrac{1}{2}{mv}^{2} = \dfrac{1}{2}m\left(- gt\right)2$

$⇒ K . E . = \dfrac{1}{2}{mg}^{2}t^{2}$

$⇒ K . E . ∝ t^{2}$

So, it is upward parabola. But after complete compression, $K . E .$ becomes zero, then ball will reshape again. Kinetic energy will not be constant.

$\frac{d y}{d x}=y+\int_0^2 y d x$

Say $\int_0^2 y d x=A \Rightarrow \frac{d y}{d x}=y+A \Rightarrow \frac{d y}{y+A}=d x \Rightarrow \ln (y+A)=x+B$
Given $y(0)=1 \Rightarrow B=\ln (1+A) \Rightarrow \ln \frac{(y+A)}{(1+A)}=x \Rightarrow y+A=(1+A) e^x$
Now find ' $A$ '
$A=\int_0^2\left[(1+A) e^x-A \left\lvert\, d x \Rightarrow A=\frac{e^2-1}{4-e^2}\right.\right.$

Hence solution $\mathrm{y}(\mathrm{x})=\left(1+\frac{\mathrm{e}^2-1}{4-\mathrm{e}^2}\right) \mathrm{e}^{\mathrm{x}}-\left(\frac{\mathrm{e}^2-1}{4-\mathrm{e}^2}\right)=\frac{3 \mathrm{e}^{\mathrm{x}}-\mathrm{e}^2+1}{4-\mathrm{e}^2}$
$\begin{aligned}
& y(2)=\frac{2 e^2+1}{4-e^2} \\
& \Rightarrow\|y(2)\|=4
\end{aligned}$

6a0e2778165ae1327797b3ba.subject: Chemistry
6a0e2778165ae1327797b3ba.text: Identify the set of coordination complexes in which all the species are diamagnetic in nature.
6a0e2778165ae1327797b3ba.sol:
In $\left[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_6\right]^{4-}$, $\mathrm{Fe}$ is in $+2$ oxidation state with a $3d^6$ configuration. Since $\mathrm{CN}^-$ is a strong field ligand, electrons pair up to give $t_{2g}^6 e_g^0$. It has zero unpaired electrons and is diamagnetic.

In $\left[\mathrm{Co}\left(\mathrm{NH}_3\right)_6\right]^{3+}$, $\mathrm{Co}$ is in $+3$ oxidation state with a $3d^6$ configuration. $\mathrm{NH}_3$ acts as a strong field ligand for $\mathrm{Co}^{3+}$, leading to $t_{2g}^6 e_g^0$. It has zero unpaired electrons and is diamagnetic.

In $\left[\mathrm{PtCl}_4\right]^{2-}$, $\mathrm{Pt}$ is in $+2$ oxidation state with a $5d^8$ configuration. For $4d$ and $5d$ series metals, the crystal field splitting is large, resulting in a square planar geometry ($dsp^2$ hybridization) where all electrons are paired. It is diamagnetic.

In $\left[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_6\right]^{3-}$, $\mathrm{Fe}$ is in $+3$ oxidation state ($3d^5$). With the strong field ligand $\mathrm{CN}^-$, the configuration is $t_{2g}^5 e_g^0$, having one unpaired electron (paramagnetic).

In $\left[\mathrm{CoF}_6\right]^{3-}$, $\mathrm{Co}$ is in $+3$ oxidation state ($3d^6$). With the weak field ligand $\mathrm{F}^-$, the configuration is $t_{2g}^4 e_g^2$, having four unpaired electrons (paramagnetic).

In $\left[\mathrm{Fe}\left(\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}\right)_6\right]^{2+}$, $\mathrm{Fe}$ is in $+2$ oxidation state ($3d^6$). With the weak field ligand $\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}$, the configuration is $t_{2g}^4 e_g^2$, having four unpaired electrons (paramagnetic).

Thus, only the first set contains all diamagnetic species.

Answer: $\left[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_6\right]^{4-}, \left[\mathrm{Co}\left(\mathrm{NH}_3\right)_6\right]^{3+}, \left[\mathrm{PtCl}_4\right]^{2-}$

$\mathrm{C_6H_5CH_2CONH_2} \xrightarrow{\mathrm{Br_2/KOH}} \mathrm{C_6H_5CH_2NH_2}$ (Q)

Benzylamine, being a primary aliphatic amine, reacts with nitrous acid (generated in situ from $\mathrm{NaNO_2}$ and $\mathrm{HCl}$) to form an unstable diazonium salt. This salt decomposes to give a benzyl carbocation, which is trapped by water to form benzyl alcohol.

$\mathrm{C_6H_5CH_2NH_2} \xrightarrow{\mathrm{NaNO_2 + HCl}} [\mathrm{C_6H_5CH_2N_2^+Cl^-}] \xrightarrow{\mathrm{H_2O}} \mathrm{C_6H_5CH_2OH}$ (R)

Answer: $\mathrm{C_6H_5CH_2OH}$

6a2109b3219e1ae5a17229ad.text: Biochemical analysis of a double-stranded DNA sample reveals that $18\%$ of its nitrogenous bases are Cytosine. Which of the following correctly represents the expected proportion of Adenine and Thymine in this sample?
6a2109b3219e1ae5a17229ad.sol:
According to Chargaff's rule for double-stranded DNA, the percentage of Adenine equals the percentage of Thymine, and the percentage of Guanine equals the percentage of Cytosine.

Given that Cytosine ($C$) is $18\%$, Guanine ($G$) is also $18\%$.

Total percentage of $C + G = 18\% + 18\% = 36\%$.

The remaining percentage for Adenine and Thymine is $100\% - 36\% = 64\%$.

Since $A = T$, the percentage of Adenine ($A$) is $\dfrac{64\%}{2} = 32\%$ and the percentage of Thymine ($T$) is $\dfrac{64\%}{2} = 32\%$.

Answer: $32\%$ Adenine and $32\%$ Thymine

6a2a77bdfad2360f42564bb2.text: The cyanide ion ($CN^-$) can bind to a metal center through either the carbon atom or the nitrogen atom, forming different complexes. Based on this property, the cyanide ion is classified as a:
6a2a77bdfad2360f42564bb2.sol:
The cyanide ion ($CN^-$) has two potential donor atoms: carbon and nitrogen. It can bind to a central metal atom or ion through either of these two atoms, but only one at a time. Such unidentate ligands that can coordinate through two different atoms are known as ambidentate ligands.

Other common examples of ambidentate ligands include the thiocyanate ion ($SCN^-$) which can bind through sulfur or nitrogen, and the nitrite ion ($NO_2^-$) which can bind through nitrogen or oxygen.

Answer: Ambidentate ligand

6a16f32a7cfacf7984f8675f.text:
Match List I with List II :

List IList II
ANatural infection by a microbeIPassive immunity
BInjection of preformed antibodiesIIPhysiological barrier
CRejection of a transplanted organIIIActive immunity
DAcid in the stomachIVCell-mediated immunity

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
6a16f32a7cfacf7984f8675f.sol:
Natural infection by a microbe leads to the production of antibodies in the host body, which is known as active immunity. Thus, A matches with III.

Injection of preformed antibodies provides immediate protection and is known as passive immunity. Thus, B matches with I.

Rejection of a transplanted organ is primarily caused by the cell-mediated immune response, which involves T-lymphocytes. Thus, C matches with IV.

Acid in the stomach acts as a physiological barrier of innate immunity by preventing microbial growth. Thus, D matches with II.

Therefore, the correct matching is A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II.

Answer: A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II

6a7a1ff8051d5249af98f91c.text: A line charge is placed along the positive x-axis. Its linear charge density varies with distance $x$ from the origin as $\lambda = \lambda_0 x$, where $\lambda_0$ is a positive constant. A hypothetical cube of side length $a$ is positioned such that one of its corners is at the origin $(0,0,0)$ and three of its edges lie along the positive x, y, and z axes. The total electric flux through the six faces of the cube is (Take $\epsilon_0$ as the permittivity of free space)
6a7a1ff8051d5249af98f91c.sol:
The portion of the line charge relevant to the cube lies along the x-axis from $x = 0$ to $x = a$.

The total charge on this segment of the line is found by integrating the linear charge density:
$q_{\text{segment}} = \int_{0}^{a} \lambda dx = \int_{0}^{a} \lambda_0 x dx = \lambda_0 \left[ \dfrac{x^2}{2} \right]_{0}^{a} = \dfrac{\lambda_0 a^2}{2}$

This segment of the line charge lies exactly on the edge of the cube (the x-axis). The dihedral angle of the cube at this edge is $90^{\circ}$, which is $\dfrac{1}{4}$ of the full $360^{\circ}$ space surrounding the line.

Therefore, the charge effectively enclosed by the cube is $\dfrac{1}{4}$ of the charge on the segment:
$q_{\text{en}} = \dfrac{1}{4} \times \dfrac{\lambda_0 a^2}{2} = \dfrac{\lambda_0 a^2}{8}$

By Gauss's Law, the total electric flux through the cube is:
$\Phi = \dfrac{q_{\text{en}}}{\epsilon_0} = \dfrac{\lambda_0 a^2}{8 \epsilon_0}$.

Answer: $\dfrac{\lambda_0 a^2}{8 \epsilon_0}$

6a7a1ff8557d5efce2d53c85.subject: Physics
6a7a1ff8557d5efce2d53c85.text: A uniform rod of length $2\text{ m}$ is placed on a smooth horizontal table and is rotated about a vertical axis passing through one of its ends at a constant angular velocity of $20\text{ rad s}^{-1}$. The density of the material of the rod is $7500\text{ kg m}^{-3}$ and its Young's modulus is $2 \times 10^{11}\text{ N m}^{-2}$. The total elongation of the rod is $x \times 10^{-5}\text{ m}$. The value of $x$ is _____.
6a7a1ff8557d5efce2d53c85.sol:
Consider an element of length $dr$ at a distance $r$ from the axis of rotation. The mass of this element is $dm = \rho A dr$, where $A$ is the cross-sectional area and $\rho$ is the density.

The tension $T(x)$ at a distance $x$ from the axis is responsible for providing the centripetal force to the portion of the rod from $x$ to $L$:
$T(x) = \int_{x}^{L} (dm) \omega^2 r = \int_{x}^{L} (\rho A dr) \omega^2 r$
$T(x) = \rho A \omega^2 \left[ \dfrac{r^2}{2} \right]_{x}^{L} = \dfrac{\rho A \omega^2}{2} (L^2 - x^2)$

The elongation $d(\Delta l)$ of a small element of length $dx$ at distance $x$ is:
$d(\Delta l) = \dfrac{T(x) dx}{AY}$

The total elongation $\Delta l$ is obtained by integrating from $x = 0$ to $x = L$:
$\Delta l = \int_{0}^{L} \dfrac{\rho A \omega^2 (L^2 - x^2)}{2 A Y} dx$
$\Delta l = \dfrac{\rho \omega^2}{2 Y} \left[ L^2 x - \dfrac{x^3}{3} \right]_{0}^{L}$
$\Delta l = \dfrac{\rho \omega^2}{2 Y} \left( L^3 - \dfrac{L^3}{3} \right) = \dfrac{\rho \omega^2 L^3}{3 Y}$

Substitute the given values:
$\rho = 7500\text{ kg m}^{-3}$
$\omega = 20\text{ rad s}^{-1} \Rightarrow \omega^2 = 400\text{ rad}^2\text{ s}^{-2}$
$L = 2\text{ m} \Rightarrow L^3 = 8\text{ m}^3$
$Y = 2 \times 10^{11}\text{ N m}^{-2}$

$\Delta l = \dfrac{7500 \times 400 \times 8}{3 \times 2 \times 10^{11}}$
$\Delta l = \dfrac{24 \times 10^6}{6 \times 10^{11}} = 4 \times 10^{-5}\text{ m}$

Comparing this with $x \times 10^{-5}\text{ m}$, we get $x = 4$.

Answer: $4$

6a7a1ff8b500b4a01871aae7.subject: Physics
6a7a1ff8b500b4a01871aae7.text: Water of density $1000 \text{ kg/m}^3$ flows through a horizontal pipe having a wide section of cross-sectional area $40 \text{ cm}^2$ and a narrow constriction of cross-sectional area $20 \text{ cm}^2$. If the pressure difference between the wide section and the narrow constriction is $6000 \text{ Pa}$, the volume flow rate of water in the pipe is:
6a7a1ff8b500b4a01871aae7.sol:
Let the velocity of water in the wide section be $v_1$ and in the narrow constriction be $v_2$.

Using the equation of continuity:
$A_1 v_1 = A_2 v_2$
$(40 \times 10^{-4}) v_1 = (20 \times 10^{-4}) v_2$
$v_2 = 2 v_1$

Applying Bernoulli's theorem for horizontal flow:
$P_1 + \dfrac{1}{2} \rho v_1^2 = P_2 + \dfrac{1}{2} \rho v_2^2$
$P_1 - P_2 = \dfrac{1}{2} \rho (v_2^2 - v_1^2)$

Substitute the given values $\Delta P = 6000 \text{ Pa}$, $\rho = 1000 \text{ kg/m}^3$, and $v_2 = 2 v_1$:
$6000 = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 1000 \times ((2v_1)^2 - v_1^2)$
$6000 = 500 \times (4v_1^2 - v_1^2)$
$6000 = 500 \times 3v_1^2$
$1500 v_1^2 = 6000$
$v_1^2 = 4 \Rightarrow v_1 = 2 \text{ m/s}$

The volume flow rate $Q$ is given by:
$Q = A_1 v_1$
$Q = (40 \times 10^{-4} \text{ m}^2) \times (2 \text{ m/s})$
$Q = 80 \times 10^{-4} \text{ m}^3/\text{s} = 8 \times 10^{-3} \text{ m}^3/\text{s}$

Since $1 \text{ m}^3 = 1000 \text{ L}$, the volume flow rate in L/s is:
$Q = 8 \times 10^{-3} \times 1000 \text{ L/s} = 8 \text{ L/s}$

Answer: $8 \text{ L/s}$

6a7a1ff83012fa2ab5a7e15a.text: A container holds a mixture of $2$ moles of a diatomic gas and $4$ moles of a monatomic gas at a temperature $T$. The ratio of specific heats $\left(\gamma = \dfrac{C_p}{C_v}\right)$ for this gas mixture is:
6a7a1ff83012fa2ab5a7e15a.sol:
The molar heat capacity at constant volume for the mixture is given by:

$C_{v,mix} = \dfrac{n_1 C_{v1} + n_2 C_{v2}}{n_1 + n_2}$

For the diatomic gas ($n_1 = 2$ moles), $C_{v1} = \dfrac{5R}{2}$.
For the monatomic gas ($n_2 = 4$ moles), $C_{v2} = \dfrac{3R}{2}$.

Substituting the values:

$C_{v,mix} = \dfrac{2 \left(\dfrac{5R}{2}\right) + 4 \left(\dfrac{3R}{2}\right)}{2 + 4} = \dfrac{5R + 6R}{6} = \dfrac{11R}{6}$

The molar heat capacity at constant pressure for the mixture is:

$C_{p,mix} = C_{v,mix} + R = \dfrac{11R}{6} + R = \dfrac{17R}{6}$

The ratio of specific heats for the mixture is:

$\gamma = \dfrac{C_{p,mix}}{C_{v,mix}} = \dfrac{\dfrac{17R}{6}}{\dfrac{11R}{6}} = \dfrac{17}{11}$

Answer: $\dfrac{17}{11}$

6a7a1ff8ac03d7c2d69d9994.subject: Physics
6a7a1ff8ac03d7c2d69d9994.text: A block of mass $m$ is attached to a light spring of force constant $k$ and executes simple harmonic motion with a time period $T$. If a graph is plotted with $\log T$ on the $y$-axis and $\log m$ on the $x$-axis, the slope of the resulting straight line is:
6a7a1ff8ac03d7c2d69d9994.sol:
The time period $T$ of a spring-mass system is given by:
$T = 2\pi \sqrt{\dfrac{m}{k}}$

Taking the logarithm on both sides, we get:
$\log T = \log \left( 2\pi \left( \dfrac{m}{k} \right)^{\dfrac{1}{2}} \right)$
$\log T = \dfrac{1}{2}\log m + \log \left( \dfrac{2\pi}{\sqrt{k}} \right)$

Comparing this with the equation of a straight line, $y = mx + c$, where $y = \log T$ and $x = \log m$, the slope of the line is the coefficient of $\log m$.

Therefore, the slope is $\dfrac{1}{2}$.

Answer: $\dfrac{1}{2}$

6a7a1ff8afc808ecbf8082e4.text: A cubical region of side $a$ contains an electromagnetic wave with an electric field amplitude $E_0$. A second cubical region of side $2a$ contains a different electromagnetic wave but holds the exact same total electromagnetic energy as the first region. If $c$ is the speed of light in vacuum, the magnetic field amplitude of the second wave is
6a7a1ff8afc808ecbf8082e4.sol:
The average energy density of an electromagnetic wave can be expressed in terms of the electric field amplitude as $u_E = \dfrac{1}{2}\varepsilon_0 E_0^2$ or in terms of the magnetic field amplitude as $u_B = \dfrac{B_0^2}{2\mu_0}$.

The total energy in the first cubical region (volume $V_1 = a^3$) is:
$U_1 = \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\varepsilon_0 E_0^2\right) a^3$

The total energy in the second cubical region (volume $V_2 = (2a)^3 = 8a^3$) is:
$U_2 = \left(\dfrac{B_0'^2}{2\mu_0}\right) (8a^3)$

Given that the total energies are equal ($U_1 = U_2$):
$\dfrac{1}{2}\varepsilon_0 E_0^2 a^3 = \dfrac{B_0'^2}{2\mu_0} (8a^3)$

Cancelling $a^3$ and rearranging for $B_0'^2$ gives:
$B_0'^2 = \dfrac{\varepsilon_0 \mu_0 E_0^2}{8}$

Using the relation for the speed of light $c = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{\varepsilon_0 \mu_0}}$, we can substitute $\varepsilon_0 \mu_0 = \dfrac{1}{c^2}$:
$B_0'^2 = \dfrac{E_0^2}{8c^2}$

Taking the square root of both sides yields the magnetic field amplitude of the second wave:
$B_0' = \dfrac{E_0}{\sqrt{8}c} = \dfrac{E_0}{2\sqrt{2}c}$

Answer: $\dfrac{E_0}{2\sqrt{2}c}$

6a7a1ff8a0d7dac53940b76d.subject: Physics
6a7a1ff8a0d7dac53940b76d.text: A light ray passes through a prism of apex angle $A$. If the angle of minimum deviation is observed to be exactly twice the apex angle, the refractive index of the material of the prism is :
6a7a1ff8a0d7dac53940b76d.sol:
The refractive index of a prism is given by the formula:

$\mu = \dfrac{\sin\left(\dfrac{A+\delta_m}{2}\right)}{\sin\left(\dfrac{A}{2}\right)}$

Given that the angle of minimum deviation $\delta_m = 2A$, we substitute this into the formula:

$\mu = \dfrac{\sin\left(\dfrac{A+2A}{2}\right)}{\sin\left(\dfrac{A}{2}\right)} = \dfrac{\sin\left(\dfrac{3A}{2}\right)}{\sin\left(\dfrac{A}{2}\right)}$

Using the triple angle identity $\sin(3x) = 3\sin x - 4\sin^3 x$ with $x = \dfrac{A}{2}$:

$\mu = \dfrac{3\sin\left(\dfrac{A}{2}\right) - 4\sin^3\left(\dfrac{A}{2}\right)}{\sin\left(\dfrac{A}{2}\right)}$

$\mu = 3 - 4\sin^2\left(\dfrac{A}{2}\right)$

Using the half-angle formula $2\sin^2\left(\dfrac{A}{2}\right) = 1 - \cos A$, we get:

$\mu = 3 - 2(1 - \cos A) = 1 + 2\cos A$

Answer: $1 + 2\cos A$

6a7a1ff832c20ccf19aa6e7e.subject: Chemistry
6a7a1ff832c20ccf19aa6e7e.text:
If $60 \text{ g}$ of ethane ($\text{C}_2\text{H}_6$) is burnt in the presence of $112 \text{ g}$ of oxygen ($\text{O}_2$), the mass of water produced is ______ g.

(Given molar masses in $\text{g mol}^{-1}$: $\text{C} = 12.0$, $\text{H} = 1.0$, $\text{O} = 16.0$)
6a7a1ff832c20ccf19aa6e7e.sol:
The balanced chemical equation for the combustion of ethane is:
$2\text{C}_2\text{H}_6 + 7\text{O}_2 \rightarrow 4\text{CO}_2 + 6\text{H}_2\text{O}$

Molar mass of ethane ($\text{C}_2\text{H}_6$) $= 2 \times 12 + 6 \times 1 = 30 \text{ g mol}^{-1}$
Moles of ethane $= \dfrac{60}{30} = 2 \text{ mol}$

Molar mass of oxygen ($\text{O}_2$) $= 32 \text{ g mol}^{-1}$
Moles of oxygen $= \dfrac{112}{32} = 3.5 \text{ mol}$

From the balanced equation, $2 \text{ mol}$ of ethane requires $7 \text{ mol}$ of oxygen for complete combustion.
Since only $3.5 \text{ mol}$ of oxygen is available, $\text{O}_2$ is the limiting reagent.

According to the stoichiometry, $7 \text{ mol}$ of $\text{O}_2$ produces $6 \text{ mol}$ of $\text{H}_2\text{O}$.
Moles of $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ produced $= \dfrac{6}{7} \times 3.5 = 3 \text{ mol}$

Molar mass of water ($\text{H}_2\text{O}$) $= 18 \text{ g mol}^{-1}$
Mass of water produced $= 3 \times 18 = 54 \text{ g}$

Answer: $54$

6a7a1ff8517d00ce03009753.text: Complete combustion of $2.9 \mathrm{~g}$ of an oxygen-containing organic compound yielded $6.6 \mathrm{~g}$ of $\mathrm{CO}_2$ and $2.7 \mathrm{~g}$ of $\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}$. If the vapour density of the compound is $29$, the number of hydrogen atoms present in one molecule of the compound is _____.
6a7a1ff8517d00ce03009753.sol:
Moles of $\mathrm{CO}_2$ produced = $\dfrac{6.6}{44} = 0.15 \mathrm{~mol}$
Moles of carbon in the compound = $0.15 \mathrm{~mol}$
Mass of carbon = $0.15 \times 12 = 1.8 \mathrm{~g}$

Moles of $\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}$ produced = $\dfrac{2.7}{18} = 0.15 \mathrm{~mol}$
Moles of hydrogen atoms = $2 \times 0.15 = 0.30 \mathrm{~mol}$
Mass of hydrogen = $0.30 \times 1 = 0.3 \mathrm{~g}$

Mass of oxygen in the compound = Total mass - (Mass of C + Mass of H)
$W_{\mathrm{O}} = 2.9 - (1.8 + 0.3) = 2.9 - 2.1 = 0.8 \mathrm{~g}$
Moles of oxygen atoms = $\dfrac{0.8}{16} = 0.05 \mathrm{~mol}$

Molar ratio of C : H : O = $0.15 : 0.30 : 0.05 = 3 : 6 : 1$
Empirical formula of the compound is $\mathrm{C}_3\mathrm{H}_6\mathrm{O}$.
Empirical formula mass = $(3 \times 12) + (6 \times 1) + 16 = 58$

Molar mass of the compound = $2 \times \text{Vapour density} = 2 \times 29 = 58 \mathrm{~g \, mol}^{-1}$

Since the empirical formula mass is equal to the molar mass, the molecular formula is also $\mathrm{C}_3\mathrm{H}_6\mathrm{O}$.
Therefore, the number of hydrogen atoms in one molecule is $6$.

Answer: $6$

6a7a1ff8cce00e45a36e30a6.subject: Chemistry
6a7a1ff8cce00e45a36e30a6.text:
Four orbitals in a multi-electron atom are described by their number of nodes as follows:



Orbital A: 2 radial nodes, 1 angular node
Orbital B: 1 radial node, 2 angular nodes
Orbital C: 4 radial nodes, 0 angular nodes
Orbital D: 0 radial nodes, 3 angular nodes



The correct increasing order of energy for these orbitals is:
6a7a1ff8cce00e45a36e30a6.sol:
The number of angular nodes is equal to the azimuthal quantum number ($l$). The number of radial nodes is given by the formula $(n - l - 1)$, where $n$ is the principal quantum number.



Let us determine $n$ and $l$ for each orbital:



Orbital A: $l = 1$. Radial nodes $= n - 1 - 1 = 2 \Rightarrow n = 4$. This is the 4p orbital. $(n+l) = 4 + 1 = 5$.



Orbital B: $l = 2$. Radial nodes $= n - 2 - 1 = 1 \Rightarrow n = 4$. This is the 4d orbital. $(n+l) = 4 + 2 = 6$.



Orbital C: $l = 0$. Radial nodes $= n - 0 - 1 = 4 \Rightarrow n = 5$. This is the 5s orbital. $(n+l) = 5 + 0 = 5$.



Orbital D: $l = 3$. Radial nodes $= n - 3 - 1 = 0 \Rightarrow n = 4$. This is the 4f orbital. $(n+l) = 4 + 3 = 7$.



In a multi-electron atom, the energy of an orbital increases with the value of $(n+l)$. If two orbitals have the same $(n+l)$ value, the one with the higher $n$ has higher energy.



Comparing the $(n+l)$ values: A (5), B (6), C (5), D (7).



Orbitals A and C both have $(n+l) = 5$. Since orbital C has a higher $n$ value ($n=5$) than orbital A ($n=4$), C has higher energy than A.



Thus, the increasing order of energy is A $<$ C $<$ B $<$ D.



Answer: A $<$ C $<$ B $<$ D

6a7a1ff886d44e7c8f51de37.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A) : Potassium permanganate ($\mathrm{KMnO}_4$) is not used as a primary standard in redox titrations.
Reason (R) : $\mathrm{KMnO}_4$ is highly hygroscopic and absorbs moisture from the atmosphere rapidly.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
6a7a1ff886d44e7c8f51de37.sol:
Assertion (A) is correct because $\mathrm{KMnO}_4$ is a secondary standard. It is difficult to obtain in a perfectly pure state and usually contains traces of $\mathrm{MnO}_2$.

Reason (R) is incorrect because $\mathrm{KMnO}_4$ is not highly hygroscopic. The primary reasons it fails as a primary standard are its instability in aqueous solution (it slowly oxidizes water), its decomposition catalyzed by light, and its reactivity with trace organic matter. Reagents like $\mathrm{NaOH}$ are the ones rejected for being deliquescent and absorbing moisture.

Answer: (A) is correct but (R) is not correct

Given below are four statements regarding s-block elements:


(A) The hydration enthalpy of $\text{Mg}^{2+}$ is more negative than that of $\text{Na}^+$.
(B) The aqueous ionic mobility of alkali metals follows the order $\text{Cs}^+ > \text{Rb}^+ > \text{K}^+ > \text{Na}^+ > \text{Li}^+$.
(C) The hydrated radius of $\text{Be}^{2+}$ is smaller than that of $\text{Ba}^{2+}$.
(D) The magnitude of hydration enthalpy decreases down the group for alkaline earth metals.


Choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
6a7a1ff8fc4811a666934686.sol:
Statement (A) is correct: Alkaline earth metal ions like $\text{Mg}^{2+}$ have a higher charge and smaller size than alkali metal ions like $\text{Na}^+$, leading to a higher charge density and a more negative hydration enthalpy.

Statement (B) is correct: Smaller bare ions are more extensively hydrated. Thus, $\text{Li}^+$ has the largest hydrated radius and consequently the lowest ionic mobility in aqueous solution, while $\text{Cs}^+$ has the highest ionic mobility.

Statement (C) is incorrect: Due to its very small bare ionic size, $\text{Be}^{2+}$ is heavily hydrated, making its hydrated radius much larger than that of the larger $\text{Ba}^{2+}$ ion.

Statement (D) is correct: As bare ionic size increases down the group, the extent of hydration decreases, causing the magnitude of hydration enthalpy to decrease.

Therefore, statements (A), (B) and (D) are correct.

Answer: (A), (B) and (D) only

6a7a1ff8895a92ca04df94c1.text: Complete reductive ozonolysis of $960 \text{ mg}$ of a hydrocarbon C yields solely $2,6$-heptanedione as the product. The volume of $\text{H}_2$ gas (in $\text{mL}$) that would be consumed by $960 \text{ mg}$ of C during complete catalytic hydrogenation at STP ($1 \text{ atm}, 273 \text{ K}$) is
6a7a1ff8895a92ca04df94c1.sol:
Since the ozonolysis of hydrocarbon C yields a single product containing two carbonyl groups, C must be a monocycloalkene.

The product is $2,6$-heptanedione: $\text{CH}_3-\text{C(=O)}-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{C(=O)}-\text{CH}_3$.

To find the structure of C, we connect the two carbonyl carbons (C2 and C6) to form a double bond. This creates a five-membered ring with methyl groups on the two carbons of the double bond.
Thus, hydrocarbon C is $1,2$-dimethylcyclopentene.

The molecular formula of $1,2$-dimethylcyclopentene is $\text{C}_7\text{H}_{12}$.
Molar mass of C $= 7 \times 12 + 12 = 96 \text{ g/mol}$.

Moles of C present $= \dfrac{960 \times 10^{-3} \text{ g}}{96 \text{ g/mol}} = 0.01 \text{ mol}$.

Since C has one double bond, $1$ mole of C consumes $1$ mole of $\text{H}_2$ gas during complete catalytic hydrogenation.
Moles of $\text{H}_2$ consumed $= 0.01 \text{ mol}$.

Volume of $\text{H}_2$ gas at STP ($1 \text{ atm}, 273 \text{ K}$) $= 0.01 \text{ mol} \times 22400 \text{ mL/mol} = 224 \text{ mL}$.

Answer: $224$

6a7a1ff845eb369d8cb8a5c8.text:
A galvanic cell is constructed using two generic metals $A$ and $B$. The cell reaction is given as:

$A(s) + B^{2+}(aq) \rightleftharpoons A^{2+}(aq) + B(s)$

The equilibrium constant $K$ for this reaction is $10^{16}$ at $298\text{ K}$. If the concentrations of the aqueous ions are $[A^{2+}] = 10^{-4}\text{ M}$ and $[B^{2+}] = 10^{-2}\text{ M}$, the actual cell potential $E_{\text{cell}}$ is ________ $\times 10^{-2}\text{ V}$.

(Given: $\dfrac{2.303RT}{F} = 0.06\text{ V}$)
6a7a1ff845eb369d8cb8a5c8.sol:
The standard cell potential $E^{\circ}_{\text{cell}}$ is related to the equilibrium constant $K$ by the equation:
$E^{\circ}_{\text{cell}} = \dfrac{2.303RT}{nF} \log K$

For the given reaction, the number of electrons transferred is $n = 2$.
$E^{\circ}_{\text{cell}} = \dfrac{0.06}{2} \log(10^{16})$
$E^{\circ}_{\text{cell}} = 0.03 \times 16 = 0.48\text{ V}$

The reaction quotient $Q$ is:
$Q = \dfrac{[A^{2+}]}{[B^{2+}]} = \dfrac{10^{-4}}{10^{-2}} = 10^{-2}$

Using the Nernst equation to find the non-standard cell potential $E_{\text{cell}}$:
$E_{\text{cell}} = E^{\circ}_{\text{cell}} - \dfrac{2.303RT}{nF} \log Q$
$E_{\text{cell}} = 0.48 - \dfrac{0.06}{2} \log(10^{-2})$
$E_{\text{cell}} = 0.48 - 0.03 \times (-2)$
$E_{\text{cell}} = 0.48 + 0.06 = 0.54\text{ V}$

Converting to the requested format:
$E_{\text{cell}} = 54 \times 10^{-2}\text{ V}$

The value is 54.

Answer: $54$

6a7a1ff8326dfbbae3c6528b.text: Let $S = \left\{ \text{Re}\left( \dfrac{z^2 - 2z + 9}{z^2 - 5z + 9} \right) : z \in \mathbb{C}, |z| = 3, z^2 - 5z + 9 \neq 0 \right\}$. Which of the following intervals correctly represents the set $S$?
6a7a1ff8326dfbbae3c6528b.sol:
Given $|z| = 3$, we have $|z|^2 = 9$, which implies $z\bar{z} = 9$, or $\dfrac{9}{z} = \bar{z}$.

The given expression is $\dfrac{z^2 - 2z + 9}{z^2 - 5z + 9}$.

Dividing the numerator and the denominator by $z$, we get:
$\dfrac{z - 2 + \dfrac{9}{z}}{z - 5 + \dfrac{9}{z}} = \dfrac{z + \bar{z} - 2}{z + \bar{z} - 5}$

Let $z = x + iy$. Then $z + \bar{z} = 2x$, where $x = \text{Re}(z)$.
Since $|z| = 3$, the real part $x$ must satisfy $-3 \le x \le 3$.

Substitute $z + \bar{z} = 2x$ into the expression:
$g(x) = \dfrac{2x - 2}{2x - 5}$

Notice that $g(x)$ is purely real, so $\text{Re}(g(x)) = g(x)$.
We need to find the range of $g(x)$ for $x \in [-3, 3] \setminus \{2.5\}$.

Rewrite $g(x)$ as:
$g(x) = \dfrac{2x - 5 + 3}{2x - 5} = 1 + \dfrac{3}{2x - 5}$

The function has a vertical asymptote at $x = 2.5$, which lies inside the domain $[-3, 3]$.
For $x \in [-3, 2.5)$, the expression $2x - 5$ takes values in $[-11, 0)$.
Thus, $\dfrac{3}{2x - 5} \in \left(-\infty, -\dfrac{3}{11}\right]$, and $g(x) \in \left(-\infty, 1 - \dfrac{3}{11}\right] = \left(-\infty, \dfrac{8}{11}\right]$.

For $x \in (2.5, 3]$, the expression $2x - 5$ takes values in $(0, 1]$.
Thus, $\dfrac{3}{2x - 5} \in [3, \infty)$, and $g(x) \in [1 + 3, \infty) = [4, \infty)$.

Taking the union of these two intervals, the range of $S$ is $\left(-\infty, \dfrac{8}{11}\right] \cup [4, \infty)$.

Answer: $\left(-\infty, \dfrac{8}{11}\right] \cup [4, \infty)$

6a7a1ff8f436c360fc33c9e7.text: Let $P$ be a point on the parabola $y^2 = 8x$ with vertex $O$. A line $L$ passing through $O$ is drawn perpendicular to the tangent at $P$. If $L$ intersects the parabola again at point $Q$, then the locus of the centroid of triangle $OPQ$ is :
6a7a1ff8f436c360fc33c9e7.sol:
For the parabola $y^2 = 8x$, $a = 2$.
Let the coordinates of $P$ be $(2t^2, 4t)$.
The slope of the tangent to the parabola at $P$ is $\dfrac{2a}{y_1} = \dfrac{4}{4t} = \dfrac{1}{t}$.

Since line $L$ is perpendicular to the tangent at $P$, its slope is $-t$.
Line $L$ passes through the origin $O(0,0)$, so its equation is:
$y = -tx$

To find the coordinates of $Q$, substitute $y = -tx$ into the equation of the parabola:
$(-tx)^2 = 8x$
$t^2 x^2 = 8x$
Since $Q$ is not the origin, $x \neq 0$, giving $x = \dfrac{8}{t^2}$.
Then, $y = -t\left(\dfrac{8}{t^2}\right) = -\dfrac{8}{t}$.
Thus, $Q = \left(\dfrac{8}{t^2}, -\dfrac{8}{t}\right)$.

Let $G(h, k)$ be the centroid of triangle $OPQ$.
$h = \dfrac{0 + 2t^2 + \dfrac{8}{t^2}}{3} \implies \dfrac{3h}{2} = t^2 + \dfrac{4}{t^2}$
$k = \dfrac{0 + 4t - \dfrac{8}{t}}{3} \implies \dfrac{3k}{4} = t - \dfrac{2}{t}$

To eliminate $t$, square the equation for $k$:
$\left(\dfrac{3k}{4}\right)^2 = \left(t - \dfrac{2}{t}\right)^2$
$\dfrac{9k^2}{16} = t^2 + \dfrac{4}{t^2} - 4$

Substitute the expression for $h$ into this equation:
$\dfrac{9k^2}{16} = \dfrac{3h}{2} - 4$

Multiply the entire equation by $16$:
$9k^2 = 24h - 64$
$9k^2 - 24h + 64 = 0$

Replacing $(h, k)$ with $(x, y)$, the locus is:
$9y^2 - 24x + 64 = 0$

Answer: $9y^2 - 24x + 64 = 0$

6a7a1ff8ce162c54ae461989.text: The number of integral values of $a$ for which the equation $\cos^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1-x^2}{1+x^2}\right) - \tan^{-1}x = a$ has exactly one real root is
6a7a1ff8ce162c54ae461989.sol:
Let $f(x) = \cos^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1-x^2}{1+x^2}\right) - \tan^{-1}x$.

We know the piecewise definition for the inverse cosine term:
$\cos^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1-x^2}{1+x^2}\right) = \begin{cases} 2\tan^{-1}x, & x \ge 0 \\ -2\tan^{-1}x, & x < 0 \end{cases}$

Thus, the function $f(x)$ can be written as:
$f(x) = \begin{cases} 2\tan^{-1}x - \tan^{-1}x = \tan^{-1}x, & x \ge 0 \\ -2\tan^{-1}x - \tan^{-1}x = -3\tan^{-1}x, & x < 0 \end{cases}$

Let us analyze the range of $f(x)$ in both intervals:
For $x \ge 0$, $\tan^{-1}x \in \left[0, \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$. The function strictly increases from $0$ to $\dfrac{\pi}{2}$.
For $x < 0$, $\tan^{-1}x \in \left(-\dfrac{\pi}{2}, 0\right)$, so $-3\tan^{-1}x \in \left(0, \dfrac{3\pi}{2}\right)$. The function strictly decreases from $\dfrac{3\pi}{2}$ to $0$.

To have exactly one real root, the horizontal line $y = a$ must intersect the graph of $f(x)$ exactly once.
From the ranges above:
- For $a = 0$, there is exactly one intersection at $x = 0$.
- For $a \in \left(0, \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$, the line intersects both branches, yielding two roots.
- For $a \in \left[\dfrac{\pi}{2}, \dfrac{3\pi}{2}\right)$, the line intersects only the $x < 0$ branch, yielding exactly one root.
- For $a \ge \dfrac{3\pi}{2}$ or $a < 0$, there are no roots.

Therefore, the equation has exactly one real root if $a = 0$ or $a \in \left[\dfrac{\pi}{2}, \dfrac{3\pi}{2}\right)$.

We need the integral values of $a$ in this set. Since $\dfrac{\pi}{2} \approx 1.57$ and $\dfrac{3\pi}{2} \approx 4.71$, the integers in the interval $\left[\dfrac{\pi}{2}, \dfrac{3\pi}{2}\right)$ are $2, 3$, and $4$.

Including $a = 0$, the possible integral values for $a$ are $0, 2, 3$, and $4$.

The number of such integral values is $4$.

Answer: $4$

6a7a1ff8b74b2da3e24c18c2.text: Let $M_n$ be the absolute minimum value of the function $f_n(x) = x^{n+2} - x^n$ on the interval $[0, 1]$, where $n \in \mathbb{N}$. Then $\lim_{n \to \infty} (n M_n)$ is equal to
6a7a1ff8b74b2da3e24c18c2.sol:
$f_n'(x) = (n+2)x^{n+1} - n x^{n-1} = x^{n-1}((n+2)x^2 - n)$.

Setting $f_n'(x) = 0$ for $x \in [0, 1]$ gives the critical point $x^2 = \dfrac{n}{n+2}$, so $x = \sqrt{\dfrac{n}{n+2}}$.

The minimum value $M_n$ is obtained by substituting this into $f_n(x) = x^n(x^2 - 1)$:
$M_n = \left(\sqrt{\dfrac{n}{n+2}}\right)^n \left(\dfrac{n}{n+2} - 1\right) = \left(\dfrac{n}{n+2}\right)^{\dfrac{n}{2}} \left(\dfrac{-2}{n+2}\right)$.

We need to evaluate $\lim_{n \to \infty} (n M_n)$:
$\lim_{n \to \infty} n M_n = \lim_{n \to \infty} \left[ \left(\dfrac{n}{n+2}\right)^{\dfrac{n}{2}} \left(\dfrac{-2n}{n+2}\right) \right]$.

This can be split into two limits:
$\lim_{n \to \infty} \left(\dfrac{-2n}{n+2}\right) = -2$.

And $\lim_{n \to \infty} \left(\dfrac{n}{n+2}\right)^{\dfrac{n}{2}} = \lim_{n \to \infty} \left(1 - \dfrac{2}{n+2}\right)^{\dfrac{n}{2}}$.

This is a $1^{\infty}$ indeterminate form. The limit is $e^L$, where $L = \lim_{n \to \infty} \dfrac{n}{2} \left(-\dfrac{2}{n+2}\right) = -1$.

So, the second limit is $e^{-1} = \dfrac{1}{e}$.

Multiplying these results, the required limit is $-2 \times \dfrac{1}{e} = -\dfrac{2}{e}$.

Answer: $-\dfrac{2}{e}$

6a7a1ff8e77d8b56bbf6f597.text: The area of the region defined by $S = \{ (x, y) : 2x^2 \le y \le 4 - 2|x| \}$ is
6a7a1ff8e77d8b56bbf6f597.sol:
The region $S$ is bounded below by the parabola $y = 2x^2$ and above by the curve $y = 4 - 2|x|$.

Since both $y = 2x^2$ and $y = 4 - 2|x|$ are even functions, the region is symmetric about the $y$-axis. We can find the area in the first quadrant ($x \ge 0$) and multiply it by $2$.

In the first quadrant, the upper curve is $y = 4 - 2x$.
To find the point of intersection of the two curves in the first quadrant, we solve:
$2x^2 = 4 - 2x$
$\Rightarrow 2x^2 + 2x - 4 = 0$
$\Rightarrow x^2 + x - 2 = 0$
$\Rightarrow (x + 2)(x - 1) = 0$

Since $x \ge 0$, the intersection point is at $x = 1$.

The area $A$ of the region is:
$A = 2 \int_{0}^{1} \left( (4 - 2x) - 2x^2 \right) dx$

Integrating with respect to $x$:
$A = 2 \left[ 4x - x^2 - \dfrac{2x^3}{3} \right]_{0}^{1}$
$A = 2 \left( 4(1) - (1)^2 - \dfrac{2(1)^3}{3} - 0 \right)$
$A = 2 \left( 4 - 1 - \dfrac{2}{3} \right)$
$A = 2 \left( 3 - \dfrac{2}{3} \right)$
$A = 2 \left( \dfrac{7}{3} \right) = \dfrac{14}{3}$

The area of the region is $\dfrac{14}{3}$ sq. units.

Answer: $\dfrac{14}{3}$

6a7a1ff872b55a6632731f95.text: Let $\vec{a}$, $\vec{b}$, and $\vec{c}$ be three unit vectors. If their resultant vector $\vec{v} = \vec{a} + \vec{b} + \vec{c}$ makes an identical angle $\theta$ with each of the vectors $\vec{a}$, $\vec{b}$, and $\vec{c}$, such that $\cos \theta = \dfrac{2}{3}$, then the value of $|\vec{a} - \vec{b}|^2 + |\vec{b} - \vec{c}|^2 + |\vec{c} - \vec{a}|^2$ is equal to
6a7a1ff872b55a6632731f95.sol:
Given $\vec{v} = \vec{a} + \vec{b} + \vec{c}$.

Taking the dot product of $\vec{v}$ with $\vec{a}$:
$\vec{v} \cdot \vec{a} = |\vec{v}| |\vec{a}| \cos \theta = |\vec{v}| (1) \left(\dfrac{2}{3}\right) = \dfrac{2}{3} |\vec{v}|$.

Similarly, since $\vec{v}$ makes the same angle $\theta$ with $\vec{b}$ and $\vec{c}$:
$\vec{v} \cdot \vec{b} = \dfrac{2}{3} |\vec{v}|$ and $\vec{v} \cdot \vec{c} = \dfrac{2}{3} |\vec{v}|$.

Now, consider the dot product of $\vec{v}$ with itself:
$\vec{v} \cdot \vec{v} = \vec{v} \cdot (\vec{a} + \vec{b} + \vec{c}) = \vec{v} \cdot \vec{a} + \vec{v} \cdot \vec{b} + \vec{v} \cdot \vec{c}$.

$|\vec{v}|^2 = \dfrac{2}{3} |\vec{v}| + \dfrac{2}{3} |\vec{v}| + \dfrac{2}{3} |\vec{v}| = 2 |\vec{v}|$.

Since $\cos \theta = \dfrac{2}{3}$, $\vec{v}$ is not the zero vector, so we can divide by $|\vec{v}|$ to get $|\vec{v}| = 2$.

Thus, $|\vec{a} + \vec{b} + \vec{c}|^2 = |\vec{v}|^2 = 4$.

Expanding $|\vec{a} + \vec{b} + \vec{c}|^2$:
$|\vec{a}|^2 + |\vec{b}|^2 + |\vec{c}|^2 + 2(\vec{a} \cdot \vec{b} + \vec{b} \cdot \vec{c} + \vec{c} \cdot \vec{a}) = 4$.

Since $\vec{a}$, $\vec{b}$, $\vec{c}$ are unit vectors:
$3 + 2(\vec{a} \cdot \vec{b} + \vec{b} \cdot \vec{c} + \vec{c} \cdot \vec{a}) = 4 \Rightarrow 2(\vec{a} \cdot \vec{b} + \vec{b} \cdot \vec{c} + \vec{c} \cdot \vec{a}) = 1$.

We need to find the value of $|\vec{a} - \vec{b}|^2 + |\vec{b} - \vec{c}|^2 + |\vec{c} - \vec{a}|^2$.

Expanding this expression gives:
$2(|\vec{a}|^2 + |\vec{b}|^2 + |\vec{c}|^2) - 2(\vec{a} \cdot \vec{b} + \vec{b} \cdot \vec{c} + \vec{c} \cdot \vec{a})$.

Substituting the known values:
$2(3) - 1 = 6 - 1 = 5$.

Answer: $5$
